dievas.subtitle: Sky-father, Dievas Senelis · pan-Baltic name; the beggar-god is folk-tale material
fields: God (Layer I) · the Crown of the World Tree, Dangus and the Glass Mountain
None. Walks the Middle World as the Beggar
None recorded or invented. Only custom: bread, coin or a story for the stranger at the door
Turning the stranger away: not punished, but left blind to your own road
An old beggar in grey rags in a whirl of wind that stirs no other leaf; a coin that opens into a grey pebble; faint blue light in his footprints in snow

sections.title: Answers
entries: He asks bread, a coin or a story. Those who give are not rescued but seen: their path becomes clear to them, even when it leads to death.
He threw the beggar a silver coin (Book I ch. 4) and walked to Krėva knowing.
He may call Vytautas Vyti, a god's licence under canon Q7.

sections.title: Refuses
entries: He never bargains and cannot be asked.
He does not act. He only sees.

sections.title: Costs
entries: To be seen is to know your road. The price is that you cannot unknow it.
What is paid for truth is worth nothing as money.

perkunas.subtitle: Thunder, oaths, justice · best-attested Baltic god; the oath-keeper role is reconstructed
fields: God (Layer I) · hardens into the Force Perkūno Rūstybė after a thousand sworn oaths
Oak groves and lightning-struck trees; the stone axe as thunderbolt; an ox or goat for oaths (Kęstutis, 1351); bread left on Thursday (late folk reckoning)
Sheltering under a tree in a storm; keeping a black cat or dog in the house; leaving doors open, where Velnias can hide. Breaking an oath
Lightning that strikes only banners and oaks; thunder like a traitor's name; dry storms with no cloud; a cracked window; the smell of ozone

sections.title: Answers
entries: Enforces the thunder oath, sworn on an axe or by a struck oak. A precise oath pleases him because exactness pleases him.
He cannot be asked through Kalba. He acts only by marking a mortal and by signs.
An oath sworn on a claimed person's name binds the Force too (Grunwald, Book III ch. 17).

sections.title: Refuses
entries: He strikes his own as readily as others. A claimed man can only keep faith.
Gives him no shelter. Perkūnas does not stop for whoever stands in front of the guilty.
He keeps oaths. That is all he is.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Kęstutis pays for every word since the ox oath (Book VI ch. 28).
When Perkūnas hunts, the village burns (legends §8).
With Jūratė and Bangpūtys. The old judgment on Jūratė is unfinished, which is why he presses Birutė's son.

perkunas.source: cosmology.md §2.1, §3.1 · magic_rules.md §7 · power_systems.md §2.6, §7 · legends_and_songs.md §1, §7, §8 · Book I ch. 1, 8, 10, 19 · wiki/gods/perkunas

velnias.subtitle: Lord of the dead, wealth and bargains · a pre-Christian god is argued, the folk devil is firm
fields: The dead, the underworld, wealth, cattle, bargains, cleverness
God (Layer I) · the Roots, Anapilis. A shard of him became the Force Šešėlių Pardavėjas
The Shadow-Seller (Henė), a splinter, not the whole god (D2)
None attested. The dead are owed their feast at Vėlinės
Naming him lightly; giving him shelter in a storm; a pact at a crossroads at midnight; shaking his hand
A gentleman in green or black with a goose-foot; black cats and dogs; warm coins; sounds that die; three blackened stones; a stranger who laughs a great deal by the fire

sections.title: Answers
entries: Anything, worded precisely. He drafts, never cheats, and keeps every deal to the letter. Free at first; the thread comes later.
He keeps them, and with them every broken oath he has bought as a debt.

sections.title: Refuses
entries: A god's bargain is iron, which is what makes him beatable by the clever.
He flees him, hiding in trees, stones and animals.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Paid later, with something worth more than you thought.
A keeper's soul goes down to his roots at death.
Beaten only by wit (the crop-division tale): turnips and rye. Nobody has beaten the neighbours.

velnias.source: cosmology.md §3.1 · canon_decisions.md D2 · magic_rules.md §8 · legends_and_songs.md §8, §9 · bestiary.md §2, §20 · wiki/gods/velnias

laima.subtitle: Spinner of fate · attested early-modern (1666); sister-goddesses and the seven spinners are folk or modern
fields: Fate, share, death (with Dalia and Giltinė)
Linen, a towel or a hen left for her in the pirtis at a birth, women only
Naming the third sister in a house with a newborn; keeping her out (the shutters are left open on the first night)
Three grey women at the edge of lamplight at a birth, spinning, measuring, shears in a lap; a cuckoo calling in winter

sections.title: Answers
entries: She spins every fate at birth, Dalia measures it, Giltinė cuts it. Her spinning is why seers see possibilities, never certainties.
A born seer at the winter-solstice midnight may ask the deivės to re-tie a thread.
Patron of Užkalbėjimai and of the Stars working.

sections.title: Refuses
entries: Her decree is a sentence, not a wall: the words are fixed, their meaning is open. She keeps her ledger to the letter.
After 1387, fates spun without a gift are plainer, with fewer surprises.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Shortens another life somewhere, by as much.
A mother may speak one word on the first night, and Laima warns it is paid for. Birutė's surety is that bill (Book VI ch. 12).

laima.source: cosmology.md §3.1 · bestiary.md §19 · legends_and_songs.md §10 · power_systems.md §2.2 · Book VI ch. 12 · wiki/gods/laima

giltine.subtitle: Death, Laima's sister · attested late (Prätorius, 1690s); the Godfather Death tale type is well documented
fields: Death: she cuts the thread Laima spins
God (Layer I) · Laima's servant and sister, never bound by the Pact
None possible. She is not asked, fed or appeased
Naming her in a house with a newborn. Turning the sick-bed works once per lineage
A tall grey or white woman with shears at the head (he dies) or foot (he lives) of a sickbed; a smell of cut grass in winter; the cuckoo falling silent

sections.title: Answers
entries: She comes to the bed. In Book I ch. 9 she stands at Kęstutis's cell door, unnamed, and does not enter.
She can be tricked once. Vytautas and Julijona turn his bed and buy days, not years (Book IV ch. 28-29).

sections.title: Refuses
entries: She cannot be bribed and does not bargain.
She is the one being unchanged by it, because death owes no courtesy.

sections.title: Costs
entries: The debt is collected at the worst moment, when the trickster's house is at its height.
A Bangpūtys working can pull a soul back from the gate, but the healer takes part of the wound.

giltine.source: cosmology.md §3.1 · bestiary.md §18 · legends_and_songs.md §10 · Book I ch. 9 · Book IV ch. 28-29 · wiki/gods/giltine

zemyna.subtitle: Earth goddess · attested (Łasicki c. 1582; Prätorius); earth-oaths and Dagotuvės are later
fields: Earth, fertility, oaths sworn on soil
God (Layer I) · her wild grief with Medeina's hardened into the Force Šaknų Motina (canon D8: not a synonym)
Earth, *Žemė tau laikys* · zenith Dagotuvės, autumn-equinox dusk
Beer poured on the ground; bread of the last harvest buried before sowing; the kissed soil of oaths; a cock or hen in the household rite (Prätorius)
Ploughing or sowing before the first thunder (late folk rule); breaking an earth-oath; burning her land
The oath-breaker's land rejects him: crops fail, horses throw him, the forest loses him; a red blister under the pouch and a cold pebble (Book I ch. 20)

sections.title: Answers
entries: Stillness and endurance on another (*tau*) or oneself (*man*). Her zenith halves the cost.
Binding physically. She patronises Priesaika alongside Perkūnas.
She keeps them in the soil to tend the fields (the kaukai).

sections.title: Refuses
entries: The one who burns the land
She turns away. After Vytautas's army burns a village she takes the first part of the debt (ch. 20).
An Earth working is impossible there.

sections.title: Costs
entries: A major Earth working turns the caster to stone for the length of the effect, and costs permanent grace.
An earth-debt, separate from any working.

medeina.subtitle: Forest and hunt · conventional reading of a corrupt 1252 chronicle entry; Łasicki's Modeina
fields: God (Layer I) · her grief fused with Žemyna's in the 13th-century crusades; merged into the Root-Mother
Šaknų Motina, who speaks with both voices
None attested in detail, and the saga assigns none: what the Root-Mother is owed (the forest kept, the axe stopped)
A hare crossing the path (Volhynian Chronicle, 1252: Mindaugas would not enter a grove)
None under her name. Her work is the swamp that eats trackers, woods that guide scouts, wolves that attack riders with foreign seals

sections.title: Answers
entries: She is never named in the books. She exists in the Root-Mother's wild, partisan grief.
The Root-Mother's servants, the Iron Wolves, were first the men who lay down in the Dykra mud after the Order emptied Sudovia.

sections.title: Costs
entries: The price is the Root-Mother's: the Amber Debt, and wolves leaving part of the soul in the bog.
No scene names or invokes her.

saule.subtitle: The Sun · attested in dainos and Jerome of Prague; amber as her tears is a saga overlay
fields: Milk at dawn to a sun-wheel (saulutė); an offering whenever amber is taken from the shore
Taking amber after a storm without an offering: it goes cold for its whole life
Amber, which is her tears; sun-wheels on lintels and vault keys; the smell of the warmth of the sun

sections.title: Answers
entries: Patron of Gintarystė. Every piece of amber is a drop of solar grief, which is why amber stores memory and carries workings.
She does not act, speak or appear.

sections.title: Refuses
entries: She wept when Mėnuo left her for Aušrinė, and asked nothing.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Amber remembers what it witnessed and answers to the truth of whoever holds it.
Cold amber for the rest of its life.

saule.source: cosmology.md §3.1 · power_systems.md §2.5 · legends_and_songs.md §7 · Book VI ch. 29 · wiki/gods/saule

menuo.subtitle: The Moon · folk daina (Rhesa, 1825); no medieval cult recorded
fields: The Moon, tides, the faithless husband
God (Layer I) · patron of Water, not its source
None recorded, and the saga adds none
Breaking a sworn oath (people swear by the Moon when afraid of breaking it)
The full moon; the phases as his wound; amber ashore at the full moon, Saulė's tears returned

sections.title: Answers
entries: His phases fix Bangpūtys's zenith: full moon, high tide, the spring ice-break.
He is not an actor but a calendar and a lesson: the oath-breaker is cut and the seducer goes free.

sections.title: Refuses
entries: He heals each month, goes back to Aušrinė, and Perkūnas cuts him again.

sections.title: Costs
entries: The Moon healed, and was cut again. A comfort after punishment, and a threat.
The saga reads Vytautas's false baptism of 1383 as his sin.

gabija.subtitle: Hearth fire · attested only in Łasicki as Gabie; the great sacred fires are not named Gabija in the sources
fields: The hearth and the sacred fire
God (Layer I) · she does not hunger, she guards
Fire, *Ugnis tau degs* · zenith Rasos, summer-solstice noon
Bread and salt; a bowl of water by the hearth; ashes over the coals at night; fire-leaping at Rasos
Spitting into the fire, stamping on it or stepping over it
A hearth that will not go out; the Šventaragis flame; a palm-sized lantern flame that silences the rain (Book III ch. 17)

sections.title: Answers
entries: Strength and warmth against the dark half of the year. At its simplest it keeps a dying flame alive.
From a sacred flame it is the strongest ward in the land.
Fire is their craft, and the vow-fire is not a fool, only exact (Book VI ch. 11).

sections.title: Refuses
entries: She cannot defend a flame no one tends.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Exhaustion for a minor working; for a major one, soul-chill, and the caster can kill without feeling.
Their sparks, cut off from her, become the užgesėlės.

bangputys.subtitle: Sea, waves and storms · attested late and thinly (Prätorius, 1690s); absent from the medieval chronicles
fields: God (Layer I) · Mėnuo sets his tides
Water, *Vanduo tau teks* · zenith full moon or high tide, strongest at the spring ice-break
Amber, or a ring given to the water. The sea may refuse it (Birutė's, Book I ch. 11)
None attested; Prätorius's one sea-rite is unreliable
A ring returned by the waves; foam; the sea's moaning in a storm

sections.title: Answers
entries: Healing, and the pull of a soul back from the gate. It can carry a thirst away or draw poison through hair and blood across distance.
The amber priestesses scry in a bowl of water with amber.

sections.title: Refuses
entries: The cost doubles away from living water, and the White Silence freezes it.

sections.title: Costs
entries: A minor Water working brings raging thirst.
A major one: the caster takes part of the patient's wound. Moving that cost into another body is forbidden, and the debt finds its owner.
He is in an old quarrel with Perkūnas over Jūratė.

bangputys.source: cosmology.md §3.1 · magic_rules.md §3.3, §4.1 · Book I ch. 11, 27 · Book VI ch. 10 · wiki/gods/bangputys

vejopatis.subtitle: Lord of the wind · attested late (Prätorius, 1690s); soul-carrier role is the saga's synthesis
fields: The four winds; messenger between worlds
God (Layer I) · the Birds' Way, the bridge of souls
Wind, *Vėjas tau neš* · zenith storms and Vėlinės
The vėlės fed at Vėlinės: food left out overnight, the pirtis heated, graves visited with fire, quiet kept in the house
Casting in a cave or still air (the cost doubles); none other attested
Fog that thickens at a Wind cry; a bird knocking at the window; the vėlės passing along the Milky Way

sections.title: Answers
entries: Real fog, swiftness and carried words. With an amber anchor distance is free.
Speech with the dead goes through him. A fed vėlė can be asked for help.

sections.title: Refuses
entries: The fog is real fog, never a glamour (Law of Truth).

sections.title: Costs
entries: A major working costs the voice: only whistling for days, and permanently with repeated use. Birutė's voice failed after the Krėva fog (Book I ch. 14-25).

vejopatis.source: cosmology.md §1, §3.1 · magic_rules.md §3.3, §4.1 · bestiary.md §15 · Book I ch. 3, 11, 14, 15, 25 · wiki/gods/vejopatis

praurime.subtitle: Fire of the stars · attested late / doubtful: known mainly from Narbutt (1835); authenticity disputed
fields: The fire of the stars; the sky-twin of the eternal flame
God (Layer I) · the saga's seers know her as the fire above, the stars read as Laima's lit threads
Stars, *Žvaigždės tau švytės* · zenith Kūčios, winter-solstice midnight
None. A starry sky is the medium; no altar. Kūčios is the seer's night: shadows on the wall, firelight in amber, the lots
Asking for what you do not truly want (Law of Truth): you get nothing, or what you do want
The cold brightness of her eyes at the end of a Five-Voice; a vision that shows a possibility, not a doom

sections.title: Answers
entries: Seeing at distance, through time as possibility and never certainty, and into the truth. Every vision shows the seer something about herself.
A Praurimė seer can see through the Shadow-Seller's illusions.

sections.title: Refuses
entries: Impossible under cloud, and doubled in daylight.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Hours for a minor working, days for a major one, or the permanent loss of one beloved face from memory.
Doubled. Birutė's vision at Dagotuvės cost two or three days (Book I ch. 3). At Kūčios, half (Book V ch. 29).

praurime.source: cosmology.md §3.1 · magic_rules.md §3.3, §4.1 · Book I ch. 3, 9, 15 · Book V ch. 29 · wiki/gods/praurime

jurate.subtitle: Queen of the amber palace · attested late (Jucevičius, 1842; Maironis, 1920); literary-romantic, kept as 1382 oral lore
fields: The sea's amber court, and its grief
God (Layer I, mythic) · first holder of the Force-office Gintaro Karalienė
The Amber Queen, an office of grief and memory (canon D1)
An offering whenever amber is taken after a storm; a ring given to the water. Wall-amber from the Šventoji mouth is too dangerous to work, since it remembers the palace
Dievai nemyli mirtingųjų: gods do not love the dying
The sea's moaning in a storm; amber on the Palanga shore after a storm; the Queen's surf-whisper through amber

sections.title: Answers
entries: She speaks only as the Amber Queen, only through amber.
Her drowned court survives as the sea-maidens.

sections.title: Refuses
entries: She cannot raise Kastytis. The Queen only keeps the dead, in memory and in amber.
She is chained to the ruins of her palace by Perkūnas.

sections.title: Costs
entries: A god who loves a mortal steals a death from Laima and Giltinė. Each vessel of her office pays it back with her mortality, a little in each generation.
The last vessel paid the remainder at Palanga in 1384.

jurate.source: cosmology.md §3.4 · canon_decisions.md D1 · legends_and_songs.md §1 · Book I ch. 27 · Book III ch. 14 · wiki/gods/jurate

root_mother.subtitle: Native Force · saga invention on Žemyna and Medeina
fields: Native Force (Layer II). Not a synonym for Žemyna (canon D8)
The wild grief of Žemyna and Medeina, fused in the 13th-century crusades, when the Order emptied Sudovia (1277-83) and she made the Dykra her body

Galminas, the dead žynys she reanimated, who becomes a grove at Grunwald. Servants: Pelkių Eglė, the Iron Wolves, the žalčiai, the barstukai, devotees such as Elena. Claim: Vytautas, contested with Perkūnas
The forest kept; plough, axe and iron stopped. She hates the knights' iron and the cities' stone
The Amber Debt, royal blood for land lost (D7). Her servants pay in parts: Eglė's price (never sell the forest), a wolf's part of the soul left in the bog, Galminas's body
Groans in the earth; roots shifting at night; sap turning red before a massacre; crows leading columns; a whisper that is leaves; soil in the mouth that smells of rain
She cannot follow onto the steppe (no forest, no bog). Consecrated stone and the axe defeat her. She fades as groves are felled

sections.title: Traits
entries: A god's attention hardened into appetite and agenda. She is bargained with, never merely petitioned, and she remembers every bargain.
She chooses not a prince but what a prince can give her (Book V ch. 11). Perkūnas also claims Vytautas.
Bog-iron is her own metal. Smith's iron and feast-day iron hurt her spirits.

sections.title: Lair
entries: The swamp-forest belt between Krėva and the Neman: bog-islands and sunken paths. Strongest wherever old forest stands unfelled, and in the oldest bog.
Open steppe, consecrated stone, felled groves. By 1411 she says she has nothing left to stop them.

sections.title: Turns by book
entries: Elena, Eglė and the swamp eat Skirgaila's trackers (ch. 12-16).
The debt of the forest falls due at Salynas (ch. 19). She is absent on the steppe (ch. 23).
Pilkoji, Galminas and Grunwald: her last great act (ch. 7-29). The mouth fills with soil that smells of rain.
She sleeps (ch. 6) and says farewell through Eglė (ch. 27).
She returns, courts Švitrigaila (ch. 11), reclaims the abandoned groves (ch. 28).

root_mother.source: cosmology.md §3.1-3.2 · canon_decisions.md D5, D7, D8 · iron_wolves.md §3 · bestiary.md (three irons) · wiki/forces/root_mother

perkuno_rustybe.subtitle: Native Force · saga invention on the oath-keeping thunderer
fields: Native Force (Layer II): justice without mercy
Perkūnas after a thousand sworn oaths: the god's attention hardened by worship, war and oath-taking into appetite and agenda
No vessel. Claimed instruments: Kęstutis, Vytautas (1382-1430). Tools: the perkūnėlis carved under a sword's grip
Claims on warriors. It acts through the claimed at moments of its choosing and punishes them for breaking their own oath
Lightning that strikes only banners and oaks; thunder like a traitor's name; dry storms with no cloud; a heavy rhythm in the fingers; the smell of ozone; a cracked window as warning
An oath sworn on a claimed person's name binds the Force too. It cannot be bargained with, only kept faith with. It is silent when nothing is owed

sections.title: Traits
entries: A claimed mortal is an instrument, not a caster. The Force does not empower at will.
It punishes the claimed for betraying its nature, as readily as foes.

sections.title: Lair
entries: Oath-places: oaks, banners, battlefields. It is strongest at the moment an oath is kept or broken before it.
When nothing is owed, it is silent.

sections.title: Turns by book
entries: Marks Vytautas at Krėva (ch. 10); the cracked window of the false baptism (ch. 19); lightning in the first battle, ambiguous by design (ch. 21).
An unspoken debt on the road (ch. 5); Skirgaila's death comes too late (ch. 16); the Vorskla verdict (ch. 26).
The renewed oath over the rusted sword (ch. 17); a kept oath rewarded at Grunwald; a single sourceless stroke over Samogitia at Rasos 1411 closes the war (ch. 29).

shadow_seller.subtitle: Native Force · a splinter of Velnias (canon D2), wearing mortal masks
fields: Native Force (Layer II). The only being in the saga that can lie and make illusions; no mortal can
A splinter of Velnias that learned to enjoy the trade
Masks: Hanulas, the Riga-born Vilnius merchant (graph: 1380-82), then Henė the jester. Masters: Jogaila (1382), Skirgaila (1387-97), Vytautas's court (from 1392), Sigismund (1429-30)
Deals, and through deals the dead (the past) to outweigh the living (the future). He serves the deal, never the man
Threads: small obligations that compound. Every bargain is kept to the letter, free at first, paid later with interest
A figure at the edge of the firelight; a voice like your own conscience (the Echo); sounds that die (the Breath of the Void); warm coins; three blackened stones; cap-bells silent while he works
Beatable only by cleverness, never strength or faith. A Praurimė seer sees through his illusions at the cost of blindness. He fears Perkūnas. He can be refused: Vytautas's no at Lutsk

sections.title: Traits
entries: Never cheats, drafts. The void under his mask is the realm of the dead seen from inside, all the past at once.
He shows off time-sight with deliberate anachronisms, such as maize in 1384 (canon Q6).
Three black stones, one cousin's bargain each, dropped as each is collected: Skirgaila's 1397, Vytautas's 1430, Jogaila's 1 Jun 1434.

sections.title: Lair
entries: Wherever a deal is being drafted: the edge of a prince's fire, a jester's stool, the Echo in a man's own head.
At Krėva in 1382, the Breath of the Void; at Lutsk in 1429-30 with a crown and a flame on the table.

sections.title: Turns by book
entries: Hanulas and the 1382 trap; the stones; the Breath at Krėva (ch. 5, 12, 14, 28, 30).
Skirgaila (ch. 1, 10, 16); all three stones in his hand at Ostrów, 1392; Skirgaila's stone falls at Kyiv, 11 Jan 1397.
Sigismund's court and the crown; the last bargain refused: the gold turns to leaves (ch. 17, 21-22, 30). Vytautas's stone falls, 27 Oct 1430.
The chain to Žygimantas; Jogaila's stone falls on 1 Jun 1434; the last unmasking (ch. 12, 19, 24).
Only his small things: the Krivis recognises a small thing of Velnias at a pact (ch. 8).

shadow_seller.source: cosmology.md §3.2 · canon_decisions.md D2, Q6, Q12 · magic_rules.md §1, §8 · hidden_immortals.md §2 · world_graph.json (hene_stones) · wiki/forces/shadow_seller

amber_queen.subtitle: Native Force · an office, not a goddess (canon D1)
fields: Native Force (Layer II) and an office of grief and memory. It has no hands and needs a living vessel
Jūratė's grief, when Perkūnas shattered her amber palace and chained her to the ruins
Jūratė (mythic first holder), Birutė (1382-84), the last. Anchors after 1384: the kneeling woman at Palanga and Vytautas's pebble. Patron of the Kęstutaičiai and the Palanga vaidilutės
Memory kept: the stories of those the other gods forgot. The sea tells her priestess for forty years that the Queen lacks land
The vessel's mortality: each vessel ends by giving it back to the sea. She never raises the dead, she keeps them in memory and amber
Surf-whisper that comes only through amber; foam on the waves; amber appearing in the hands of the lost; eyes gone sea-dark; the sea returning a ring three times
Once Birutė is spent she cannot walk again. Her reach is only touched amber. Consecrated stone dampens it, and Church men want the statue gone

sections.title: Traits
entries: Everything gods and men have destroyed. Not the same as Jūratė: it spread through the sea and became something that is not her any more.
Drawn from the Palanga amber-priestess line. Birutė is the last.
The son of the last vessel carries the unpaid half of an old judgment.

sections.title: Lair
entries: The shore, the sea and any amber Birutė touched. Birutė's full-moon working at Palanga (ch. 27) is correctly timed on the Water zenith.
She acts only through amber Birutė already touched: the pebble and the kneeling statue.

sections.title: Turns by book
entries: The Queen heard through amber (ch. 3); widowhood and sea-dark eyes (ch. 11); the amber kneeling woman (ch. 27); the frame narration.
Her voice at sea before Grunwald (ch. 14).
Polish clergy come for the statue (ch. 8).
Her silence (ch. 25); her last working, spent on the dying Flame-Keeper (ch. 29); the sea takes the statue.

iron_saint.subtitle: Vulture Force · an egregore of the Order, not the Christian God
fields: Egregore (Layer II): institutional appetite wearing faith's clothes. The saga never judges the Christian God
Crusade, the Reise season, indulgence and forced baptism, and thousands of prayers in the Marienburg church of the Virgin
Patron of the Order's leaders: Zöllner (1382-90) and Jungingen (1407-10). Servants: the Reise riders and the Nedegintieji
Total homogeneity: the wild and pagan as a sickness to be purged, the world orderly and silent
Pity. It grants fearlessness, tireless marching and absence of pity; such knights cannot weep
Furnace heat in winter; the smell of quench-water; crosses that ring like anvils; ice melting on shields; snow blackening where steel steps; metal and peat smoke along the border
Earth's Unmovable Will and Fire's terror find no grip on its knights, but it can be broken: at Grunwald the white-cloaked knights lay down their swords and weep

sections.title: Traits
entries: Iron forged by a Christian smith on a holy day is tempered by appetite, not faith. The Iron Saint gathers in it, and whoever wields it is noticed.
Enforced among the Order's men. The Order distrusts converts who swore on pagan forms first.

sections.title: Lair
entries: Consecrated stone is its home ground: Kalba costs double there and amber goes cold. The cellars of Marienburg stay warm for a hundred years.
At the Reise, when thousands of prayers and marches are poured into one battle.

sections.title: Turns by book
entries: The warm cellars (ch. 11), the siege (ch. 22), its death at Grunwald (ch. 20, Geležies Mirtis).
Silenced in the North among the dying Order (ch. 14).
First met at Strėva, 1348 (ch. 7), and Rudau, 1370 (ch. 24), where Kęstutis recognises its signs.

iron_saint.source: cosmology.md §2.2, §3.3 · magic_rules.md §9 · bestiary.md (three irons), §24, §25 · power_systems.md §3 · wiki/forces/iron_saint

white_silence.subtitle: Vulture Force · an egregore of bought baptism
fields: Egregore (Layer II). Jadwiga at her best is its victim, not its servant
Purchased purity: baptisms bought or sold for land and crowns
Jadvyga (1386-99), a saint only because it uses her as a conduit. Fed by Poland and the Algirdaičiai. Servants: the bebalsiai
The Order's absolute dominion; the world bleached of pagan colour. Quiet and stillness as a state of grace
Warmth and sound. It grants fearlessness, holy calm, healing with frost and the Crusader's Winter of early snows
Frost flowers on blades and windows that grow slowly like someone writing; sound dying; lilies on frozen fields; breath white in summer
It smothers Wind and freezes Water, but warmth beats it: frost melts when a man weeps. A living flame counters it

sections.title: Traits
entries: Wherever a baptism is being bought: Jogaila's Vilnius in 1382 (he is already pricing a crown) and Krėva, where the 1385 union is signed.
Its victims are the bebalsiai, who lose voice, shadow and warmth.

sections.title: Lair
entries: Vilnius, Krėva, Kraków. Strongest in winter and wherever a bought baptism is read aloud.
An unnamed cold fills Trakai once the Last Flame goes out (Book V ch. 4).

sections.title: Turns by book
entries: Krėva first, as frost in November 1382 (ch. 14); at the 1385 union frost ferns grow on the glass and the quill makes no sound (ch. 28b).
The church at Vilnius (ch. 3); Jadvyga's frost on her hands and her child's lips, July 1399 (ch. 21).
Jogaila's frozen hand on the stone (ch. 3).
Frost in Jogaila's rooms (ch. 19); frost melts when a man weeps (ch. 14).
The unnamed cold fills Trakai (ch. 4). It is the last of the four to become pure institution.

white_silence.source: cosmology.md §3.3 · canon_decisions.md D8, D11 · hidden_immortals.md §5 · bestiary.md §26 · power_systems.md §3 · wiki/forces/white_silence

steppe_hunger.subtitle: Vulture Force · an egregore of the horizon-kings, not Tengri
fields: Egregore (Layer II). The Golden Horde's shadow, steppe name Erdene-Chuluu, jewel-stone. Not a real faith's deity
Conquest without end and the hubris of horizon-kings who think they can conquer the horizon
Patron of Edigu, who keeps a kamė that still speaks with the earth. Fed unwittingly by Vytautas's papal crusade against the Tatars. Tokhtamysh is its broken guest
Dissolution: the walls of civilisation broken, the world turned back to unmapped grassland of blood and horse-hair; a battlefield that is an altar of dust
The army, and then the king's sense of limit. The Vorskla slaughter and Edigu's mass executions are the harvest
Dust devils that walk beside the columns without wind; horse-hair crammed into wells; grass that goes yellow overnight and looks the way eyes look; a stone baba with no mouth facing east; a red sky
It cannot follow into forests or bogs, and the Root-Mother cannot follow into it. Its lures work only on those who already want an empire

sections.title: Traits
entries: A vision of an endless empire. It works only on those who already want one.
He wins by drawing a plan on the ground and wiping it out with his foot to leave no traces.

sections.title: Lair
entries: Strongest on open grassland, beyond forest and bog. Strongest of all at the Vorskla in August 1399.
Wherever there is a forest or a bog to stop it.

sections.title: Turns by book
entries: The Pope's crusade against the Tatars raises Vytautas's price (ch. 20); the march into the steppe, dust devils and red sky (ch. 23); Edigu and the kamė (ch. 24); the slaughter at the river, 12 Aug 1399 (ch. 25-26).

gold_glutton.subtitle: Vulture Force · an egregore of ledgers and tolls, Mercator-Rex
fields: Egregore (Layer II). Grows wherever appetite gathers, including in Lithuanian hearts
Ledgers, tolls, land sold by the furlong, and counting-houses: the Hanseatic ones and, from 1411, Poland
Patron of Oleśnicki (from 1411). Servant: the Counter. Fed by the Hanse and Poland
Profit: the landscape as a resource, men as ledger entries. It lends and asks for a pledge, usually a word not yet spoken
A prosperity that empties people out. It drives the sale of Samogitia for silver and the theft of the crown
Coins that are always warm; a counting voice in quiet rooms; the warmest place in a room being the coin that is never touched
It can only count what exists. A word not yet spoken cannot be bought: Vytautas's refusal to let the Last Flame die is the one entry it cannot enter

sections.title: Traits
entries: Its voice: soft, pleasant, counting geese, barrels, pearls and wheel-turns. Vytautas carries it for thirty years like a pebble in the boot.
At Lutsk the crown is turned to leaves and the Gold-Glutton writes a zero in its ledger.

sections.title: Lair
entries: Tollhouses, commanderies, Hanseatic factories, Kraków. Strongest wherever money changes hands and dominant in Book IV.
Rooms where something is given away without counting.

sections.title: Turns by book
entries: Present from the start, at the massacre and the Hanseatic merchants (ch. 7, 28).
Dominant: Sigismund's debts (ch. 17), the crown with the borrowed third (ch. 21), the last bargain (ch. 22), the zero (ch. 30).
The feast and the voice among the lords (ch. 17, 21).

kalba.subtitle: Senovės Kalba · the Ancient Tongue, asked power, bound by the Three Laws
fields: Asked power. The rarest and strongest school, and the only one that reaches across distance (through amber)
Tier 2 minor workings in one element; tier 3 one or two elements; tier 4 all five. Vytautas is bound tier 2 (the Five-Voice and the pebble only)
One line in Old Lithuanian naming an element, a recipient and a verb of giving. *Tau* is cast on another, *man* on oneself at lighter cost
A sacred medium, the words aloud (a whisper will do), and true intent. Paths: born (prigimtis), noticed (pažymėtas), bound (surištas)
Every working shows its bill: blindness, exhaustion or soul-chill, the patient's wound, petrification, loss of voice. A surety pays part of another's price
A candle's length for a minor working, a night for a major one. Hard ceiling: a castle, a night
No illusions, no raising the dead, no creating love, no changing the past, no winning a war. Fails against one who knows your true name better than you
Consecrated stone (the cost doubles, amber goes cold); the Iron Saint's fearlessness; the White Silence (smothers Wind, freezes Water); the Order's sword; a gag

sections.title: Effect
entries: Clear Sight (Stars), Soul Armour (Fire), Life Spring (Water), Unmovable Will (Earth), Shadow Speed (Wind). Each has its god, medium and zenith.
They can still use it. The gods do not care about creed, they care about truth.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: Speaking all five lines together calls a little of every boon at once. The cost is a little of every price, permanent and cumulative: dimmer sight and hearing, frayed memory. The only permanent cost a minor working can carry.
At its element's zenith the cost is halved. Off it, doubled. Some are impossible.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: Balance (*Kiek paimi, tiek atiduok*), Truth (no glamours), Memory (the land remembers every working).
A cost can be deferred, never refused, and deferred costs compound: memory first, then health, years of life, madness, death.

uzkalbejimai.subtitle: Užkalbėjimai · spoken charms, Kalba's humble cousin
fields: Asked power · folk word-magic that needs no gift
Tier 1 · žiniuonis, midwife, village healer. Thousands in 1382
The exact words, whispered three or nine times, learned from a living teacher
A medium: water, bread, salt, linen thread or a knife. Taught only to a younger person of the opposite sex [Record]
The charmer takes a trace of what is removed: a headache, a cold hand, a nightmare
One ailment or danger at a time. A house-ward against fire lasts a night
One person, one ailment. Cannot work a mortal wound alone. Fails against someone who does not believe they are being helped
Disbelief; a charm told to the wrong person (it dies for the teller); the Unbinding's unbound spirits are what charms now hold off

sections.title: Effect
entries: Stops bleeding, draws snake venom, calms a horse, takes away fright (išgąstis), wards a house from fire.
The peasantry's chief defence against unbound spirits. Priests condemn it, village priests quietly use it.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: A bleeding-charm over a Rasos-herb poultice heals mortal wounds that Water cannot.
Healers who charm too much grow strange.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: A charm told to the wrong person stops working for the teller.
A charm said for money works at half strength.

uzkalbejimai.source: power_systems.md §2.2, §4, §7 · Law of Truth, magic_rules.md §5.2 · wiki/magic/uzkalbejimai

zenklai.subtitle: Ženklai · carved signs, stored intention
fields: Asked power · the way to enchant objects
Tier 0 can use a fed sign; tier 2 (burtininkas, sign-carver) makes warded objects
Carve, burn, weave or embroider the sign, then feed it
The sign, and a feed: blood for a strong sign, milk for a gentle one, ash for a binding one
The feed. A sign fades if not fed
A charm-object (one sign) fades in a season. A warded object (several signs, fed by an owner) lasts a lifetime
A sign carved by a baptised hand works only if the carver means it. On iron it is twice as strong but angers the laumės
Neglect (it fades); consecrated stone (half strength, if meant); a broken sign reverses for a night

sections.title: Effect
entries: Saulutė repels night spirits (milk at dawn). Perkūnėlis wards lightning and marks an oath (blood, once). Žalčiukas warns of poison (milk weekly). Laimos medis eases childbirth.
Žvaigždutė helps sight-workings. Žirgeliai turn aside unbound spirits. Mėnulio pjautuvas hides by distraction, not illusion (ash).

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: Signs plus a Kalba working plus blood make an artifact. Kęstutis's sword carries a perkūnėlis under its grip.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: The rust on Kęstutis's sword is the sign failing because the Pact is cracking.

zenklai.source: power_systems.md §2.3, §5 · Book I ch. 2 · Book VI ch. 1, 4 · wiki/magic/zenklai

zoles.subtitle: Žolės · herb-lore: brews, smokes and poisons
fields: Asked power in the family list, but no gift and no Law of Balance. Power anyone can carry
Tier 1 · žolininkė, midwife. Eglė practises it at tier 3
Gather, brew, smoke. Rasos herbs are picked on solstice night before dawn, without speaking
Wormwood (kietis), St John's wort (jonažolė), sweet flag, mugwort, linden, chamomile, valerian, henbane (drignė), poppy
No magical cost. The seer's smoke costs a terrible headache. The price is moral
Rasos herbs have double potency and keep a year
Mundane: it works as chemistry. Needs no gift, and no gift improves it

sections.title: Effect
entries: Sleep (Ona's draught), truth-loosening, fever-breaking, wound-cleaning, and the seer's smoke: henbane and amber dust, which lets a Kalba seer see further.
A Rasos-herb poultice and a bleeding-charm heal what Water cannot.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: The herb-lore of princes. Skirgaila's death (1397) and the hostage sons' poisoning (1392, a contested tradition from Grunau, canon Q11) are herb-lore, not sorcery: henbane, kietis and sugar.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: That is why it is the most dangerous: the horror is how little magic the world needs.

zoles.source: power_systems.md §2.4, §4 · canon_decisions.md Q11 · Book I ch. 12 · Book II ch. 4, 9, 16 · wiki/magic/zoles

gintaryste.subtitle: Gintarystė · amber-craft, the universal medium
fields: Asked power · Saulė's grief as the medium all five elements accept
Tier 4 works it fully (the Palanga line, Birutė). Any bearer can release charged amber with the right word (tier 0)
Breathe a working into amber. Anchoring adds the caster's blood
Amber from the shore, taken with an offering; the caster's blood for an anchor; a word to release
The anchoring caster pays for every working done through the anchor: Birutė paid in voice and sight from Palanga. Amber taken after a storm without an offering goes cold for its whole life
Charged amber holds until released. An anchor holds until a second one breaks it
One anchor per caster at a time. Amber answers to the bearer's truth, not belief
Consecrated stone chills it; the Order's Bernsteinmeister burn charged amber in consecrated furnaces; the Order's sword

sections.title: Effect
entries: Raw amber carries any working. Charged amber is released later by the bearer. Anchored amber links caster and bearer across any distance. Memory amber takes a last memory from one who dies holding it.
The pebble: warm when freely given, a faint light in the dark, dead at the false baptism, burning at Žemyna's price, hot at an honest choice, glowing at a baptism honest about its dishonesty.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: With an anchor distance is free, so Birutė reached Krėva from Palanga. Her bill was her voice and sight.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: Shore-amber taken without an offering stays cold for life. Hanseatic merchants carry boxes of dead amber and never know.

gintaryste.source: power_systems.md §2.5 · magic_rules.md §3.4, §5.3-5.4 · Book I ch. 3, 14-25, 19, 20, 23, 29 · wiki/magic/gintaryste

priesaika.subtitle: Priesaika · oath-binding by blood, earth and word
fields: Asked power · an oath with the right form is literally binding
Anyone who swears with the right form. The Krivis (tier 4) and tier 3 priests conduct oaths
Swear. Earth oath: kiss or eat soil. Thunder oath: on an axe or by a lightning-struck oak. Blood-brotherhood: shared fate
Soil, an axe or a struck oak, blood. Patrons: Perkūnas and Žemyna
None at the swearing. The keeper pays by keeping (Kęstutis, Book VI ch. 28), the breaker by forfeit
An oath cannot be sworn by one who does not mean it: it rings false. Gods keep to the letter, and take by the spirit
Christian oaths on relics are enforced by the Iron Saint among the Order's men, which is why the Order distrusts converts who swore on pagan forms first

sections.title: Effect
entries: The breaker's own land rejects him: crops fail, horses throw him, the forest loses him.
Perkūnas enforces it. Lightning seeks the breaker.
Counts as an oath: Skirgaila's broken safe-conduct of August 1382.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: An oath sworn on a claimed person's name binds the Force too: Vytautas swears to Perkūnas before Grunwald, so Perkūnas must act.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: Lightning, a rejecting land, the loss of the god's favour in war. Perkūnas's enmity toward Skirgaila's line follows the broken safe-conduct.

priesaika.source: power_systems.md §2.6, §7 · magic_rules.md §5.2 · legends_and_songs.md §11 (18) · Book I ch. 1, 2, 8 · Book VI ch. 13, 28 · wiki/magic/priesaika

claim.subtitle: Žymė · the claim, granted power from a god or Force
fields: Granted power. The mortal does not initiate and does not consent
No tier: the claimed is an instrument, not a caster (a vessel is tier 5)
None. The god or Force marks the mortal
None from the mortal. The mark is felt: a rhythm in the fingers, a smell of ozone or sap, eyes that catch lightning; sometimes a scar
Until the work is done. The mark lets go
The claimed is not empowered at will. The Force acts through him at moments of its choosing. It makes no sorcerer
A claim can be contested (Perkūnas and the Root-Mother both claim Vytautas). An oath sworn on a claimed name binds the Force too

sections.title: Effect
entries: Vytautas becomes the hand of justice and oath. Perkūnas rewards him when he keeps faith and strikes when he breaks it (Book I ch. 10, 19, 21).

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: A claimed man who betrays the Force's nature is struck: the cracked window, the Vorskla verdict.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: The Vorskla defeat is partly Perkūnas's verdict on Vytautas's oath-breaking (Book II ch. 26).

claim.source: magic_rules.md §1, §7 · power_systems.md §3, §4 · Book I ch. 10, 19, 21 · Book II ch. 5, 26 · wiki/magic/claim

wolf_change.subtitle: Vilkų krikštas · the Wolves' Baptism, granted by the Root-Mother
fields: Granted power, bound by the Root-Mother's nature, not the Three Laws
Outside the practitioner tiers (the graph rates Jonas and the Flame-Keeper tier 3). Only the Seniai, twenty years sworn, can put on the wolf

The rite, held in the twelve nights after Kūčios: a wake as if he had died, his name whispered to the fire, a throat-mark rubbed with live ash, nine nights without fire, the drowning in the bog, the oath on the skull
A sworn sponsor (the vilktėvis), a sacred flame, bog-iron belt and knife, the oldest bog, the Iron Wolf's skull. Unmarried men of 16 to 25
His true name, the road up (laid in the bog, never burned), his hearth, part of his soul, a little memory each iron hour, his tears
For life. New wolves can be made only at a living flame, so the brotherhood ends when the last flame goes out in 1430
No sleep under a lit roof; the iron hour (a battle-frenzy of about an hour) takes a memory each time; the Root-Mother's healing fails on feast-day iron
Feast-day iron; consecrated stone; the hungry dead, who are drawn to a wolf like moths to a lantern

sections.title: Effect
entries: The sight of the dvasios, night-sight and scent, the Root-Mother's healing, cold and wet as nothing, pack-sense, the iron hour. It is not shape-change.
Peasants think all vilkatai become wolves. Only the Seniai can put on the wolf.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: Real flesh, granted by the Root-Mother. Each time they come back less. The last time, they do not come back, and run into the Dykra on four feet.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: Rule 2 of the Pack's Word: breaking it gives the wolf to the Root-Mother at once. He goes into the bog alive.
Every wolf in the Dykra hears it.
Once, if someone who knew his true name speaks it at a living flame and offers bread on a knife-point. He loses every gift and ages the years in one winter.

wolf_change.source: iron_wolves.md §4-7 · power_systems.md §3 · canon_decisions.md D10 · Book III ch. 7, 9 · Book V ch. 29 · wiki/magic/wolf_change

iron_gift.subtitle: The Iron Saint's fearlessness · granted power
fields: Granted power from the Iron Saint, an egregore of the Order
Tier 3 in the graph: Zöllner (from 1382), Jungingen (from 1407)
None from the knight. Thousands of prayers, indulgences and Reise marches poured into one battle do the work
Real belief or appetite, and an institution to feed it. The creed does not matter
Pity dies. Such knights cannot weep
For the battle. It can be withdrawn all at once
Needs the appetite of an institution behind it. Faces become those of men who feel nothing
Only the Force's own death, at Grunwald, and the weeping that follows. It counters Earth's Unmovable Will and Fire's terror

sections.title: Effect
entries: Fearlessness, tireless marching, absence of pity, and immunity to Earth's terror and Fire's terror. Signs: furnace heat in winter, quench-water, crosses that ring like anvils.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: Whoever wields it is noticed by the Iron Saint. It is tempered by appetite, not faith.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: At Grunwald a knight lowers his sword and tears come, then another, then a third (Book III ch. 20).

iron_gift.source: power_systems.md §3 · magic_rules.md §9 · cosmology.md §3.3 · Book III ch. 11, 20 · Book VI ch. 7, 24 · wiki/magic/iron_gift

white_touch.subtitle: The White Silence's frost-touch · granted power
fields: Granted power from the White Silence
She lays on a hand. It is not hers to command: the Force's will wearing her hands
Warmth leaves the healer: a week unable to get warm, two days of a cold aura. The child's lips go white. Sound dies around her
A sore closes overnight (Book II ch. 21)
She does not choose when. It is a cold that spreads
Warmth, such as tears (Book IV ch. 14); a living flame. Its own touch smothers Wind and freezes Water

sections.title: Effect
entries: Holy calm, closed wounds, the ending of fever. Frost fern-patterns grow where her hands lie.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: Frost passes into those who kiss her hand: Jogaila carries it afterwards (Book III ch. 3, Book IV ch. 19).

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: A žaltys tells Jadvyga that the Silence will freeze your heart while it saves your soul (Book II ch. 21).

white_touch.source: power_systems.md §3 · hidden_immortals.md §5 · Book II ch. 21 · wiki/magic/white_touch

bargain.subtitle: Sandėris · the bargain, bought power
fields: Bought power. Binds by the letter, never by the Three Laws
Tier 0: anyone desperate. Either party may initiate, but the human is rarely informed
A deal worded precisely. Velnias never cheats, he drafts. Free at first, the thread comes later
The letter of the deal; a figure at the edge of the firelight, warm coins, three stones
Paid later with interest: something worth more than you thought. Deferred costs compound
Until the bargain is collected: Jogaila's ran from 1380 to 1434
The Shadow-Seller alone can lie and make illusions. A bargain can say only what it says
Cleverness, never strength or faith (the crop-division tale). A Praurimė seer sees through illusions at the cost of blindness. Refusal: Vytautas at Lutsk

sections.title: Effect
entries: The easy way: a secret treaty, a key to a dungeon, a poison that leaves no trace. Every gift comes with a thread.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: A small favour, then a larger one. Jogaila's line inherits the crown and loses the land; Skirgaila is used and discarded.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: Plant turnips, then rye. But beating the devil does not protect you from people.
A word not yet spoken cannot be bought. The crown turns to leaves.

bargain.source: magic_rules.md §1, §8 · power_systems.md §3 · legends_and_songs.md §9 · Book I ch. 19 · Book IV ch. 22 · wiki/magic/bargain

el_stars.subtitle: Žvaigždės tau švytės · Clear Sight, the Stars working
fields: Stars · deity Praurimė (attested late / doubtful), with Laima, whose threads the seer reads
Tier 2 (minor, one element) or 3 and up. Birutė (tier 4) cast it; Vytautas has only the Five-Voice
*Žvaigždės tau švytės* aloud, a whisper is enough. *Man* for oneself
A starlit sky; true intent. Zenith Kūčios, winter-solstice midnight (about 13 December in 1382, not the Christian 24th)
Minor: hours of blindness. Major: blind for days, or the permanent loss of one beloved face from memory
A candle's length to a night
Shows branches, never a fixed trunk. Impossible under overcast, doubled in daylight
Overcast; consecrated stone (cost doubles); the Order's sword

sections.title: Effect
entries: Seeing at distance, through time (as possibility) and into the truth. Every vision shows the seer something about herself.
A Praurimė seer can see through his illusions, at the cost of blindness.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: Doubled. Birutė's vision in Book I ch. 3 fell at Dagotuvės and cost two or three days of blindness.
Halved. Book V ch. 29: the price was half, and still everything.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: Ask for what you do not truly want and you get nothing, or what you do want.

el_stars.source: magic_rules.md §3.2-3.3, §4.1 · cosmology.md §3.1 · Book I ch. 3, 9, 15, 27 · Book V ch. 29 · wiki/magic/el_stars

el_fire.subtitle: Ugnis tau degs · Soul Armour, the Fire working
fields: Fire · deity Gabija, the hearth and sacred fire. Zenith Rasos, summer-solstice noon
Tier 2 (minor, one element) or 3 and up; the craft of the vaidilutės who tend the sacred flames
Minor: exhaustion. Major: soul-chill, empathy gone for days; the caster can kill without feeling
A candle's length to a night
Doubled in rain or floods; consecrated stone doubles it. A sacred flame cannot guard itself
Rain and flood; consecrated stone; the Iron Saint's knights, who are immune to Fire's terror

sections.title: Effect
entries: Warming, kindling, bracing the spirit against the dark half of the year. At its simplest it keeps a dying flame alive.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: The chill climbs from the fingers: legs, elbows, shoulders, and a gap where something was (Book II ch. 2, 11; Book IV ch. 3).
In the half-flooded island foundations the spring damp doubles the cost, and Birutė is no longer there to share it (Book II ch. 2).

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: Spitting into the fire or stepping over it is sacrilege.

el_fire.source: magic_rules.md §3.3, §4.1 · cosmology.md §3.1 · bestiary.md §27 · Book II ch. 2, 11 · Book IV ch. 3 · wiki/magic/el_fire

el_water.subtitle: Vanduo tau teks · Life Spring, the Water working
fields: Water · deity Bangpūtys (attested late), with Mėnuo setting his tides. Zenith: full moon or high tide, strongest at the spring ice-break
Tier 2 (minor, one element) or 3 and up; the sea-craft of the amber priestesses
Running or sea water; amber for scrying in a bowl; true intent
Minor: raging thirst. Major: the caster takes the patient's wound in part
A candle's length to a night
Cannot heal a mortal wound. Doubled away from living water, in caves and at distance
The White Silence freezes it; consecrated stone; the Order's sword

sections.title: Effect
entries: Healing and the pull of a soul back from the gate. It can carry a thirst away or draw poison out through hair and blood across distance.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: After Vorskla Vytautas casts *Vanduo man teks* on a wounded boyar: the thirst vanishes, a side that was not his passes into him, and part of the pain stays (Book II ch. 27).

Moving the cost into another body, a second person or a child, is forbidden and costly: the debt finds its owner. In Book II ch. 9 the Lagoon ragana says she could draw the poison from the hostage boys, but her old body cannot carry it, so it would go into an Order child. Vytautas answers no.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: A cost shifted into another body finds its owner (magic_rules §4.1).

el_water.source: magic_rules.md §3.3, §4.1 · Book I ch. 11, 27 · Book II ch. 9, 27 · Book VI ch. 10-11 · wiki/magic/el_water

el_earth.subtitle: Žemė tau laikys · Unmovable Will, the Earth working
fields: Earth · deity Žemyna. Zenith Dagotuvės, autumn-equinox dusk (about 14-15 September)
Tier 2 (minor, one element) or 3 and up; the last Samogitian žynys Kantaudas cast it at Salynas (Book II ch. 19)
*Žemė tau laikys* aloud. *Man* for oneself holds more firmly, but only me
Minor: stiffness. Major: petrification for the length of the effect, and a permanent loss of grace
A candle's length to a night
Impossible at sea or in the air. The earth remembers the working as residue
The Iron Saint's knights are immune to Earth's terror; consecrated stone doubles the cost; the sea and the air

sections.title: Effect
entries: Stillness and endurance, a will that does not bend. Cast on another it holds him.
Vytautas, fleeing, says *Žemė man laikys*: he goes rooted and heavy, his horse freezes and a patrol's eyes slide off him (Book II ch. 27).

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: Kantaudas turns to river-stone from the hand upward before the oak the axemen fell at Salynas: let it take me, let them see what they are cutting (Book II ch. 19).

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: Žemyna's price for desecration is separate from any working. After a village burns, a red blister and a cold pebble (Book I ch. 20).

el_wind.subtitle: Vėjas tau neš · Shadow Speed, the Wind working
fields: Wind · deity Vėjopatis (attested late). Zenith: storms and Vėlinės
Tier 2 (minor, one element) or 3 and up. Birutė's Krėva fog is tier 4 through an amber anchor
Open air with wind; with an amber anchor, distance is free
Minor: vertigo. Major: loss of voice, only whistling for days, permanent with repeated use
A candle's length to a night: the Krėva fog hid a castle for a night
The fog is real fog, never an illusion. Doubled in caves and still air
The White Silence smothers Wind (no sound, no far-speech); consecrated stone

sections.title: Effect
entries: Fog, swiftness, carried words. Speech with the dead goes through Vėjopatis.
Cast from Palanga through the pebble at Wind's zenith, since the escape falls on the eve of Vėlinės (Book I ch. 14).

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: Birutė's voice fails after the Krėva fog (Book I ch. 14-25). The vessel's declining body is the bill.
After 1384 Vytautas pays the full price himself: *Vėjas man neš* after Vorskla (Book II ch. 27).

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: Forbidden under the Law of Truth. Wind makes real fog, never a false face.

silent_pact.subtitle: Tylioji Sutartis · the Silent Pact of 1345, the series engine
fields: Pact between two princes, the gods and the spirits of place. Saga invention (canon D7)
Binds Algirdas, Kęstutis and the Gediminid line. The Krivis (tier 4) is witness, not envoy
Sworn on Vėlinės night 1345 in the Šventaragis valley: iron laid on a stone, each prince whispers his secret name to the fire, blood on a Palanga amber bead, each states what he gives
A sacred flame, the Krivis, amber, blood, the princes' true names. Witnesses: every spirit of place, laumės as surety
The Amber Debt: royal blood for every land lost to the plough and cross. No one asked the children
1345 to 1387 formally; a remnant (the Hidden Groves) to 1417; folklore from 1430
A treaty between the land's people and the land's spirits, not a god's grace. The gods hold a baptised land only by custom

sections.title: Effect
entries: Lithuania will not be conquered. The Order may raid and burn but never hold the heartland.
The sacred flames are never extinguished; no Gediminid sheds Gediminid blood; the Amber Debt.
The Pact keeps the dvasios courteous.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: At Palanga in 1384 she pays the debt partially and buys the Hidden Groves, a remnant protection over Samogitia and the deep Dykra.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: Kęstutis is murdered by kin at Krėva: the gods' protection lapses.
Jogaila puts out the Šventaragis flame, fells the grove and has the sacred snakes killed. The Pact formally ends, and the Unbinding begins.
Samogitia is baptised 1413-17 and the groves fall. Vytautas dies in 1430 and the last flame goes out.

sutartis_birute.subtitle: Senovės Sutartis · Birutė's binding of Vytautas, Book I ch. 3 (1382)
fields: Birutė binds at tier 4. Vytautas, bound-2, gets the Five-Voice and the pebble and nothing else
Birutė cuts her palm with a crescent vaidilutė knife and presses the pebble into his hand, speaks his true name, and exchanges promises
Amber charged by the binder (the pebble); the binder's blood; the bound one's true name; an unbreakable promise both ways
Surety (*laidas*): part of every price Vytautas incurs is paid by Birutė, wherever she is. In 1384 she pays the whole remaining debt at once
Surety until Book I ch. 27 (1384). The bond itself, and the pebble as its barometer, until 1430
One anchor per caster. The pebble answers to the bearer's truth. After 1384 there is no surety: he pays full price
Consecrated stone deafens the pebble; the Order's sword closes the Five-Voice; a binder's own death

sections.title: Effect
entries: Hers: *Jo skola, mano skola* (his debt is my debt). His: *Kol aš gyvas, paskutinė ugnis neužges* (while I live, the last fire will not go out).
Lets an ungifted bearer call a little of every boon.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: Voice failing after the Krėva fog, sight going, until ch. 27 at Palanga.
Book II ch. 2: the spring damp doubled the cost, and Birutė was not beside him.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: Loss of gift, curse of the elements, memory loss, madness, death in the extreme.
Failure of the promise means letting the flame die while he lives.

flame_promise.subtitle: Kol aš gyvas, paskutinė ugnis neužges · the Last Flame promise
fields: Pact · Vytautas's half of the Sutartis. Saga invention
Bound tier 2 · Vytautas. Keepers: Kalvis, Spyglys, the Flame-Keeper Žiežirba; Elijas guards the vault door
Spoken in Book I ch. 3 (1382); kept from 1387 by tending a secret flame
A sacred flame: lit in Kęstutis's old lodge beyond the Neris, moved to the Trakai island foundations, and from 1392 in the vault. Live ash fed in pinches
Every pinch of ash taken is a risk to Vytautas. Fire workings at the flame cost double in damp or flood
One man cannot re-swear a Pact. The flame goes out only when he dies or lets it
Henė's offer: the crown for the flame (Book IV ch. 21-22)

sections.title: Effect
entries: While it burns, the Pact's remnant and the vilkatai's oath have a living anchor. New wolves can be made only at a living flame.
The only ward that holds the unburned dead and calms the Quenched.

sections.title: At greater cost
entries: At Lutsk the offer comes with a pledge, his word not yet spoken. He refuses, and the crown, which never existed as gold, turns to leaves. He dies uncrowned.

sections.title: Breaking it
entries: If it goes out while he lives
The Pact's penalties fall: madness, then death.
It goes out at the moment he dies, 27 Oct 1430, as a pot taken from the stove goes quiet (Book IV ch. 29). The brotherhood can make no more wolves, and the pebble cracks.

pebble.subtitle: Motinos gintaras · Birutė's pebble, anchor and barometer
fields: Bound to Vytautas by the Sutartis (amber, the binder's blood, his true name, a promise both ways). An ungifted bearer can use the Five-Voice through it. It asks only truth, not belief
Birutė (maker, 1382) → Vytautas 1382 to 27 Oct 1430 → Pilkoji 27 Oct to 24 Dec 1430 → the Flame-Keeper (Žiežirba) from Kūčios 1430 to March 1450
An anchor between bearer and Birutė (1382-84). Carries the sea and, for those she chooses, her voice. Carries the Five-Voice. Moral barometer
Answers to the bearer's truth, not belief. Consecrated stone deafens it, so costs double near Order castles and cathedrals. Silent while Vytautas carries the Order's sword

sections.title: Properties
entries: A pea-sized lump of cloudy, honey-coloured Palanga amber, worn smooth, on a leather thong. By Book V a hairline crack, visible from one angle only.
Warm when freely given. A faint light in the Krėva cell. Dead at the false baptism at Tepliava, 21 Oct 1383. Hot at the Marienwerder burning, July 1384. Glowing in 1387.
Cold after Vorskla (1399). A single tremor in 1405. Warm at the Grunwald oath, burning at the lightning (1410). Neither warm nor cold at the Black Sea.
A second bead from the same shore lies on Vytautas's slab. The first bead of that pair went to Sofija's son in Moscow.

sections.title: Curse or cost
entries: Birutė pays part of every price Vytautas incurs until she pays the whole at Palanga in 1384. After that there is no surety.
It does not flatter. It goes cold when he lies to himself, and dead when the oath is false.

sections.title: Fate
entries: It cracks like thin ice at his death on 27 Oct 1430. Pilkoji takes it from his chest and gives it to the Flame-Keeper at Kūčios.
He first looks through the crack at Rasos, June 1432. It stays dead on the flame in the crypt. Birutė's voice through it ends at his name.
It burns with him at Palanga, March 1450.

kneeling_woman.subtitle: Klūpančioji · the amber kneeling woman of Palanga
fields: Cannot be borne. Whoever moves her dies at sea
None. She is held by no one: she kneels at the tide line at Palanga from 1384. She anchors the Amber Queen 1384 to 1450
The Amber Queen's last anchor on land. She calms storms along that shore. Warm to the touch, light as a sleeping child; her glow tracks how well she is remembered
Whoever moves her dies at sea. Gifts of bread or fish are left for her whenever amber is taken from the shore. She dims as people forget her story

sections.title: Properties
entries: A human-sized kneeling woman of honey-coloured amber with insects and grains of sand suspended inside. Head bowed, hands clasped, face like candle wax. Fishermen tie ribbons to her neck.
Left where Birutė vanished into the sea at Palanga on the night of the Amber Sacrifice, 1384, the payment of the Amber Debt that bought the Hidden Groves.

sections.title: Curse or cost
entries: In October 1417 the priest Andžej Radzimski takes six men to remove her. Hammers fail, the boat sinks calmly, and she is back at dawn with six crosses in her hands (Book IV ch. 8).
In 1445-46 the village forgets, and she goes grey.

sections.title: Fate
entries: March 1450: she glows the evening the Flame-Keeper tells his stories and is the pyre's site.
The sea takes the statue (Book V ch. 29). By 1553 she is memory and tale.

kestutis_sword.subtitle: Šerno kalavijas · Kęstutis's boar-pommel sword
fields: A warded oath-blade. It keeps its bearer's word under Perkūnas's eye while the perkūnėlis is clean, and recognises its bearer each morning
Kęstutis (forged c. 1330) to 15 Aug 1382 → Skirgaila 1382 to 11 Jan 1397 → the Iron Wolves 1397 to spring 1400 → Vytautas spring 1400 to 27 Oct 1430 → unknown after 1430
A warded oath-blade: the instrument of Vytautas's blood-oath at Grunwald (14-15 Jul 1410)
Rust spreads along the blade with every oath broken in the family. After Grunwald a thin bright silver line from guard to point survives

sections.title: Properties
entries: A broad sword with a boar's head on the pommel, a perkūnėlis (thunder-cross) burned into the metal beneath the grip by Kęstutis himself. It hung over the Trakai hall stairs.
Rust begins with the cracks of 1380 and the Pact failing. Counted breaches: Dovydiškės, Skirgaila's safe-conduct, Vytautas's false baptism, the Order oath, Lyck, the Vorskla.

sections.title: Curse or cost
entries: The rust is the family's broken oaths written on the blade. Vytautas leaves it unpolished: Rūdys yra sąskaita, rust is the account (Book III ch. 2).

sections.title: Fate
entries: Skirgaila's men take it at the gate when Kęstutis is disarmed. It goes into one of twelve oak chests at Kyiv, 11 Jan 1397, and passes to the wolves; Vytautas has it from spring 1400.
The rust stops spreading after the Grunwald oath. It stands by the door at his death. After 1430 no fate is given.

silver_wolf.subtitle: Sidabrinis vilkas · Kęstutis's silver wolf, the brotherhood's sign
fields: Belongs to the brotherhood, not to the holder. It must pass hand to hand, bread for bread. Every sworn vilkatas recognises it
Kęstutis 1345 to 1382 → Vytautas 1382 to 27 Oct 1430 → Pilkoji 27 Oct to 24 Dec 1430 → the Flame-Keeper from Kūčios 1430 to March 1450 → Rimgailė of Palanga from 1450
An identity token. Carries no spell of its own. The Order's border guards, and Jogaila, read it too
Not the holder's to give away: Vytautas cannot offer it to the Dykra himself. Its meaning dies with the pack

sections.title: Properties
entries: A silver wolf a hand long with a raised snout and a worn coat, old pagan patterns along its flank, and under the belly a small second mark: a wolf's head without a collar. By Book V a tooth is broken and the silver blackened in the hollows.
Cast in the Dykra in 1345 from the silver of three drowned knights and given to Kęstutis by the Wolf-Father Kuolas after the Pact (Book VI ch. 5).

sections.title: Curse or cost
entries: Jogaila cannot hold its gaze, because he knows what the sign means (Book I ch. 26).
Kęstutis passes it to Vytautas through the gap beneath the Krėva wall: let the wolf stay with the wolf (Book I ch. 8).

sections.title: Fate
entries: Pilkoji gives it to the Flame-Keeper at Kūčios in the circle of fourteen wolves, who touch it one by one, Kirmėlė last (Book V ch. 7).
In March 1450 he gives it to Rimgailė at Palanga, bread for bread, and she puts it under her threshold. It is an heirloom in 1553 and seen on the keeper's neck in a vision (Book V ch. 29-30).

golden_chain.subtitle: Auksinė grandinė · the strangling chain, a Henė-bargain object
fields: The wearer slowly stops sleeping. It does not exhale until it has been in the room where the dead man died

Jogaila (sent as a gift with Hanulas's envoys, summer 1382) → Skirgaila 1383 to 11 Jan 1397 → Henė 1397 to Apr 1429 → Baltramiejus Rogala 1429-30 → Kraków treasury 1430-38 → Henė Aug 1438 → Žygimantas Kęstutaitis to 20 Mar 1440
Carries the Breath of the Void. Strangles without a mark, then lets its wearer hear the dead man's last breath. Muffles sound around the wearer, Henė's signature
A Henė-bargain object, kept to the letter. Masses said over it wash the wearer, not the gold

sections.title: Properties
entries: A heavy chain of Riga gold, each link perfectly welded and colder than the last. At the clasp a small mark: two crossed keys under a cross, the sign of Riga. It is warm when worn.
Fitted round Kęstutis's neck in the Krėva cell on 15 Aug 1382 (Book I ch. 9).

sections.title: Curse or cost
entries: The wearer slowly stops sleeping. Rogala wears it silent at the Noteć ford, and the chain has not yet learned to exhale (Book IV ch. 20, 23).
It lets Žygimantas hear Kęstutis breathe, and know he is not alone (Book V ch. 22).

sections.title: Fate
entries: Henė fetches it, stoneless, to the Krėva cell on 14-15 Aug 1438 and Žygimantas puts it on. It turns to dust at his murder at Trakai, 20 Mar 1440 (Book V ch. 19, 22).

ember.subtitle: Paskutinė žarija · the Last Flame, the Šventaragis ember
fields: Held to Vytautas's promise, *Kol aš gyvas, paskutinė ugnis neužges*. Others keep it by feeding ash; he alone is its bearer

Vytautas 1387 to 27 Oct 1430, with keepers: Kalvis 1387-99; Spyglys 1399-1410; the Flame-Keeper Žiežirba (a boy at the flame from c. 1396, keeper from 1405 to 1430). Elijas keeps the vault door 1398-1411
The last of the Gediminid sacred flames. Anchors the Pact's remnant and the vilkatai's oath: new wolves can be made only at it. A pinch of its ash is a lamp or a weapon, and a ward against užgesėlės
If it goes out while he lives, the Pact's penalties fall on him. Every pinch of ash taken is a risk to him

sections.title: Properties
entries: A palm-sized yellow flame with no smoke that does not bend in a draught, on a black ring of stone, fed in pinches with live ash. Where it burns, the wolves cannot sleep.

Lit in Feb-Mar 1387, the night Jogaila's priests put out the Šventaragis fire. Vytautas lights it from the ember he carried out of the valley, in Kęstutis's old hunting lodge beyond the Neris (Book I ch. 29).

sections.title: Curse or cost
entries: Madness, then death, if he lets it die while he lives. Henė offers the crown for the flame (Book IV ch. 22). He refuses.
Fire workings at it cost double in spring flood (Book II ch. 2).

sections.title: Fate
entries: The lodge, 1387. The half-flooded Trakai island foundations (Book II ch. 2). The island undercroft from autumn 1392, moved by boat on the night the keys are handed over (II ch. 11).
A horn lantern to Grunwald, 8 Jun 1410 to spring 1411 (Book III ch. 15, 17, 20). Back in the vault, like a bird on a nest.
27 Oct 1430, at the moment of Vytautas's death (Book IV ch. 29). The lightning-fire at his funeral cannot make wolves (Book V ch. 20).

order_sword.subtitle: Kryžiaus kalavijas · the Order's consecrated sword
fields: A free act is needed to be rid of it: Vytautas must put it in fire himself. While he carries it, he is the Order's vassal and his pebble cannot answer
Vytautas Oct 1383 (from Zöllner at his baptism) to July 1384. No other holder
Consecrated metal. It dampens Kalba around it: the pebble cannot answer, his blood feels strange and his Five-Voice is closed to him
Smothers amber and fire. As the replacement of Kęstutis's sword it bears no history, only a debt

sections.title: Properties
entries: A heavy straight German sword with a cross-shaped hilt, consecrated at Marienburg, smelling of cold steel and a new religion.
Presented by Zöllner at Vytautas's baptism as Wigand at Tapiau (Tepliava), 21 Oct 1383, made by the Order for its protégé.

sections.title: Curse or cost
entries: It knocks his thigh on the Order's march into Lithuania. With it he fights his first battle against his own people (Book I ch. 20, 21).

sections.title: Fate
entries: July 1384: at Marienwerder (Naujapilis) he unbuckles it and throws it into the burning tower. The pebble lights and the silence lifts (Book I ch. 23-24).

three_stones.subtitle: Henė's three black stones · the cousins' bargains
fields: Singular (a set of three, each one a cousin's bargain)
Henė alone juggles them: Jogaila's, Skirgaila's and Vytautas's. A stone shows a deal in progress
Henė 1380 to 1 Jun 1434. Stones in hand: three (1380) → two (Skirgaila's falls, 11 Jan 1397) → one (Vytautas's falls, 27 Oct 1430) → none (Jogaila's drops, 1 Jun 1434)
Each stone shows one cousin's bargain in progress. Its fall marks the collection of that bargain
Each falls when its cousin's deal is collected. Once his hands are empty, Henė has no leverage left and unmasks (Book V)

sections.title: Properties
entries: Three black, worn, round stones like river pebbles, but not from a river. Two fly true and the third always wobbles. When he is working, the cap-bells are silent and the stones make no sound.
Made 1380, the year of Dovydiškės. The first deal is with Jogaila at Krėva in 1382: the easy way, the crown for his line, the land lost.

sections.title: Curse or cost
entries: He keeps bargains to the letter. *I never lie; I only write it down.*

Skirgaila's falls through the floor at Kyiv like falling into water. Vytautas's falls in the death chamber, and Henė throws it into Lake Galvė at dawn on 28 Oct 1430: no splash, a film of ice parts and closes.

sections.title: Fate
entries: Jogaila's drops on the floor of his deathbed room on 1 Jun 1434 and does not roll: an ordinary river pebble. After 52 years Henė's hands are empty (Book V ch. 12).

wolf_skull.subtitle: Geležinio Vilko kaukolė · the Iron Wolf's skull, the brotherhood's oath-stone
fields: A wolf lays both hands on it and swears the nine laws of the Pack's Word. Its keeper, the Wolf-Father, is chosen by the Root-Mother in the bog
Lizdeika 1323 → the vilkatai 1323 to 1450: Wolf-Father Kuolas (1345), Šešiapirštis (to 1392), Pušis (1405-15), Pilkoji, the Vilkų Motina (1415 to 2 Nov 1449)
The brotherhood's oath-stone. A lie spoken over it is heard by every sworn wolf from the Neman to the Narew
Rules sworn on it, such as *no Gediminid blood*, bind even the guilty. A wolf is laid in the bog, never burned, and the skull goes down last

sections.title: Properties
entries: A skull too large to be a man's or any wolf's, grey as old iron, light enough to lift with two fingers. In Book VI ch. 18 it is cracked, with a round hole through one eye socket. It rests on a flat stone or pine stump on a bog-island in the Dykra.
Found by Lizdeika where the dream-wolf stood after Gediminas's dream, hard and grey as iron. He carried it into the Dykra, and the packs swore on it.

sections.title: Curse or cost
entries: Every wolf in the Dykra hears a lie spoken there.
It anchors the Iron Wolf, the omen of the Gediminid house.

sections.title: Fate
entries: On Vėlinės, 2 Nov 1449, Pilkoji carries it to the deepest water and lies down with it on her chest. The bog closes over her. With it goes the last office of the brotherhood (Book V ch. 28).

lutsk_crown.subtitle: Nematoma karūna · the crown that was never gold
fields: Cannot be borne. It was never gold, and no man ever wore it
None. Henė holds it in the graph for 1430: a gold crown in a gold-painted oak chest, carried north from Buda in summer 1430
None, except as a lure. The instrument of Henė's last bargain at Vytautas's vault: the crown for the flame
Henė never lies; the word *no* turns the gold to leaves. The price of the refusal is the crown itself

sections.title: Properties
entries: A gold crown in a gold-painted oak chest. When the chest is opened at the Noteć ford it holds dry leaves. The goldsmith's apprentice Pál (19) swears he held real gold.

The Congress of Lutsk, Jan 1429, where Sigismund offered Vytautas a crown. The crown itself was never seized: the embassy was held at Frankfurt (Oder) and Sigismund's courtiers were robbed on the border before 19 Aug 1430.

sections.title: Curse or cost
entries: The offer comes with a pledge: Vytautas's word, not yet spoken. He refuses.
The Gold-Glutton writes a zero in its ledger.

sections.title: Fate
entries: A crown will travel toward him all his life and never arrive (Book VI ch. 12; legends §10).
Vytautas postpones the coronation and dies uncrowned on 27 Oct 1430. On 1 Nov an old woman tells it as a tale: he died with a crown, only an invisible one.
