zaltys.subtitle: Household guardian · Baltic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] household grass snake, fed with milk (Jerome of Prague via Piccolomini; Długosz, 1387) · [Saga] the children of Žilvinas's spilled blood
Dvasia · the Root-Mother's ear inside the house
I nuisance before 1387 → III dangerous after
Under the threshold, warm straw by the oven, the cowshed
Milk in a clay bowl at the threshold, daily; to be left alive
Milk (even the baby's, in a hungry spring); in return it tells the forest everything it hears
A healthy one is seen often and fearlessly. A žaltys that hides is a warning. After 1387: snakes crossing a road in a long line, all toward the forest
None that kill it. Juniper smoke and feast-day iron drive it off, and the luck goes with it

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk are right that killing it kills the luck. They are wrong that it is harmless: it cannot hurt anyone directly, but it can withdraw, and a house it leaves goes sick, barren and quarrelsome within a year. The priest who calls it a demon is wrong too.
When Eglė's brothers cut Žilvinas down, his blood went into the ground and the grass snakes of the land were born from it. The living owe them. Eglė's own žaltys is the eldest.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Takes the house's luck with it when it goes.
Once the sacred snakes of Šventaragis are slaughtered, many leave houses in a body. Those that stay drink cows dry at night and coil in cradles beside nursing mothers.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Feeding it is not charity. In a hungry spring the žaltys's milk is the baby's milk.
Carry it to the forest edge in clean linen with a crust of bread and ask it aloud. It may refuse.
Wealth for life, and every žaltys in the parish hunts the thief's kin.

zaltys.source: bestiary.md §1 · legends_and_songs.md §2, §12.3 · cosmology.md §4.3 · Book I ch. 15-16, 23, 29

aitvaras.subtitle: Fire-tailed thief · Baltic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] wealth-spirit hatched from an old rooster's egg, named in 16th-century church writings · [Saga] hatchling of Velnias's root-wealth
Under the oven as a black cockerel or cat; a fiery streak at dusk outdoors
Scrambled eggs (kiaušinienė), fed by its keeper; fire
Grain, milk and silver from neighbours. At the keeper's death, his soul goes down to Velnias's roots with the rest of the wealth
Fiery streaks from a poor farm to a rich one; a neighbour who prospers in a bad year; eggshells by the oven; singed feathers
None kill it. Sell it on, set it an endless count (a sack of poppy seed), or burn your own farm

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk are right that it steals and burns. They are wrong that it serves the devil: it serves the trade, and anyone who feeds it. It makes no wealth, it moves it, so every grain it brings is a grain a neighbour lost.
Aitvarai turn arsonist. Near Hanseatic towns the Gold-Glutton courts them and they carry warm coin instead of grain, which starts quarrels wherever it is spent.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Carries stolen wealth from the poor farm to the rich one.
Spoil its dish and it burns the house.

sections.title: Costs
entries: The neighbours' enmity, and eventually a lynching. In life the household slowly stops being able to give anything away freely.
The buyer inherits the risk. While it counts, it is still yours.
It drops its load on your land, and the stolen goods are in your barn when the owner comes looking.

kaukas.subtitle: Field-luck · Baltic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] small bearded household and field spirit (barzdukai), named with aitvarai in 16th-century church writings · [Saga] the unnamed dead
Dvasia · kept in the soil by Žemyna
Under the threshing floor and in granary corners
Porridge on the threshing floor at harvest, and a place
Nothing at first. After 1387, the grain it once multiplied
A grain-bin that stays fuller than it should; tiny footprints in flour
Clothes (a funeral: it is released to climb); a mother naming it

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk say unbaptised infants. The truth is unnamed: babies who died before their mother spoke the secret name cannot climb the Glass Mountain, so Žemyna keeps them in the soil to tend the fields. A kaukas is the family's own dead child working the family's field.
The folk nickname, often misapplied to the barstukai. A peasant leaving porridge for the barzdukai may be feeding the wrong creature.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Increases what is already there instead of stealing.
With no courtesy owed, the unnamed dead eat the grain they once multiplied. Granaries rot from the inside.

sections.title: Costs
entries: The mother speaks a name over the threshing floor and burns a lock of her hair. The kaukas goes up to Dausos, and she loses the memory of that child's face (Law of Balance).
The field's luck goes with it.

barstukai.subtitle: Under-elder miners · Prussian and Samogitian folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] small under-elder beings of Puškaitis, attested in 16th-century Prussian and Samogitian accounts; link to kaukai debated · [Saga] the Root-Mother's diggers
Elder thickets on old hill-forts and by bogs; the dark under hill-forts
Bread and beer under the elder at dusk, never watched
Wells and mine-shafts, after 1387, from lords who drain and mine the land
Lumps of bog-iron left on a stump; hammering underground at night
Smith's iron drives them down; feast-day iron kills them

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk mix them up with kaukai, which is half right: both are small and live in earth. But a kaukas is your dead, and a barstukas is nobody's.
Bog-iron for bread, amber for beer, a safe path for a promise. The vilkatai's bog-iron comes from them.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Mine bog-ore and buried amber in the roots of elder thickets.
Stop trading and bring down wells and shafts under drainers and miners.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Watching the offering ends the bargain for the whole family.
Ask three times, or the ground under your house goes hollow.
Smith's iron sends them down, and your bog-iron with them.

slogutis.subtitle: The presser · Baltic nightmare belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] nightmare spirit that sits on sleepers' chests and rides horses by night · [Saga] a shard of a living person's grudge
Dvasia · born of a living mind, no patron named
Sleepers' chests; stables; crowded courts and camps full of resentment
To press: breath and rest from the one the sender hates
Sleep and breath. After 1387 it kills infants and the old
A heavy weight on the chest at the edge of sleep; braided horse-manes; a neighbour who looks bruised and exhausted next day
A blade at the bedside; every hole stopped; the salt trick

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk are right that it is a living soul. They are wrong that only witches send it: the jealous sister-in-law, the cheated neighbour and the bitter old soldier all do, and wake tired without knowing why.
In a court full of resentment (Jogaila's Vilnius, 1382) the sloguciai are thick as moths.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Sits on the sleeper's chest so he cannot breathe or move.
Rides horses at night and leaves them sweating, manes braided into knots.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Blade up. Children roll onto it.
In winter a sealed, smoky hut is its own danger.
Say aloud *Ateik rytoj druskos*. Whoever comes to borrow salt is the sender. Now you have a feud, and you must give the salt.

slogutis.source: bestiary.md §5 · Book I (Jogaila pressed nightly after ch. 7)

laumes.subtitle: Weavers by the water · Baltic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] beautiful long-haired water women with hen's feet, spinners and linen-washers, Thursday-evening taboo · [Saga] the weavers of custom
Dvasia · custom-bound; surety and direct witnesses of the Silent Pact
Rivers, meadows, lakes and swamps; midnight by the water
Diligence and courtesy: a hank of flax by the water at Rasos; no spinning on Thursday evening
The curious, blinded or drowned. After 1387, the babies they once swapped
Paddle-beats at midnight; wet linen on meadows at dawn with no one about; hen-tracks in the dew; a rainbow ending at a lake (laumės juosta)
Iron does little. Courtesy is the only real ward

sections.title: Traits
entries: The diligent see kindness. The truth is a law of work and courtesy, neither kind nor cruel, which looks like cruelty to everyone else. Thursday is Perkūnas's day, and a woman spinning then spins against the laumės' own wheel.
Every courtesy between the land's people and its spirits is a thread they spin. The Silent Pact is their great tapestry.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Weave and beat linen at night by the water.
Reward the diligent and orphaned; blind or drown the lazy and the watchers.

sections.title: Costs
entries: A laumė's linen never runs out, so you can never sell it.
The curious are blinded or drowned.
Laumės who once swapped babies now drown them, and their endless linen becomes shrouds.

laumiukai.subtitle: Changelings · Baltic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] children left in the cradle by laumės: big-headed, ever-hungry, never growing · [Saga] a bargain enforced without consent
Children whose mothers broke courtesy, or who were born on a laumės' night, to raise as weavers
The infant. After 1387 nothing is left: an empty cradle, or a linen-wrapped log
A baby who changes overnight: eyes too old, appetite too great, never crying at the right times; wet hen-tracks by the cradle
A knife or broom under the cradle; Laimos medis fed with the mother's hair; the secret name whispered at birth

sections.title: Traits
entries: The swap is real. What the laumė leaves is sometimes her own sickly child, but often a dying human child from another house that she is trying to save. The cruel folk remedies work because they offend custom so badly that she returns the stolen child, which means torturing a child who may be someone else's.
The child is often returned at seven, trained and strange.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Takes the infant, leaves its own in the cradle.

sections.title: Costs
entries: A mother who cannot leave the cradle cannot work the fields.
Carved on the cradle and fed with a thread of the mother's hair. It fades if unfed, and a tired mother forgets.
A named child is far harder to take, but the name is now known to the elements and to anyone who overhears.
You may be beating somebody else's baby.

vandenis.subtitle: Lake-keepers · Baltic and Slavic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] lakes and rivers that demand a drowning a year; undinė probably a later borrowing · [Saga] each lake is an eye of the World Tree
Dvasia · the drowned; the sea's jūrų mergelės answer faintly to the Amber Queen
Deep lakes no one has sounded; the sea's edge; a spot where the ice never closes
One life a year to see through
A drowning that can be chosen, not avoided. After 1387 many, and at the spring ice-break whole carts go through
A pale face just under the surface at dusk; ice that never closes; a village avoiding one shore in early summer
Salt poured in a line along the shore holds a vandenis in the water for one night

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk are right about the annual drowning. They are wrong that it can be avoided: it can only be chosen.

Every lake is an eye of the World Tree, and an eye must be kept open. The drowned become its vandeniai and look up at the world through the water. The sea-maidens are the remnants of Jūratė's drowned court.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Bread or a black rooster shortens the wait. It does not replace the death.
The old sometimes walked in to spare the young.
Holds it one night, for a fortune in salt.
A loaf with a candle finds the body so it can be burned, and the lake is then owed again.

vandenis.source: bestiary.md §8 · cosmology.md §1 · Book I ch. 11 (the ring returned three times) · Book V ch. 22

zaltvyksles.subtitle: Bog-lights and treasure-flames · Baltic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] straying lights as souls (some of dishonest surveyors); treasure that shows itself as a flame · [Saga] both belong to Velnias's ledger
Dvasia · Velnias's ledger of cheated boundaries and debts
Bogs and meadows at night; a field flame on Rasos or Vėlinės
Followers to join their measuring; buried debts paid
Travellers who follow. A treasure's claimant: a death in the finder's family within the year
Lights that move against the wind; a flame in a field that throws no heat
Do not follow. Turn your coat inside out to break the pull

sections.title: Traits
entries: Both folk stories are true. Bog-lights are the dead who cheated on boundaries and debts, walking the lines they falsified. Treasure-flames are wealth buried with a curse or bargain, still owed to the roots.
Once the Order and the new lords measure land by the furlong (the Gold-Glutton's appetite) the lights multiply. Over Samogitia after 1398 they walk in rows, like surveyors.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Following a light means joining its measuring.
Taking a treasure means taking on its debt.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Throw a shirt on the flame and do not look back. A death follows in the family within the year, and the money is warm.
Costs nothing, if you remember in time.

baubas.subtitle: Told terror · Baltic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] bogeys that frighten children (*Baubas ateis!*); the maumas of wells; the booming bittern · [Saga] made of telling
Dvasia · born of speech, no patron named
A dark corner children will not look at; a well that booms at night
To be told: each threat feeds it
The fear that settles in the corner; in the end, the family that fed it
A corner children avoid; a well that booms; a shape that matches whatever the household fears most

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk are right that it exists. They are wrong to think they are only pretending.
Real in proportion to how often it is invoked. Worst in households that have lost their other spirits.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Each time a mother says the baubas will come, a little fear settles in the dark corner. A family that threatens its children nightly feeds a real thing that eventually comes.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Stop using it as a threat. Then you need another way to keep children from the well.
Laughter, light and a pet-name cost nothing, which is why grown-ups forget them.

girinis.subtitle: Grove-keeper · Baltic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] forest guardians (girinis, miškinis, medinis) and the sacred groves (alkai) · [Saga] the local face of the Root-Mother
Dvasia · a shard of the Root-Mother
One grove, one wood, one ancient oak; the oaks of the alkai are the Pact's pillars
To be asked: bread and salt on a stump, *Leisk, medi*, and never more than you asked for
The greedy, led in circles until they die. A felled grove's girinis becomes a homeless hunger on the axeman's family
Silence where there should be birdsong; paths that return to the same stump; a branch that falls exactly where you stood
Clothes turned inside out if lost; the axe that felled a sacred oak thrown into running water

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk see a stern host. The truth: it cares about people only as they affect the trees. Each oak of the alkai felled loosens the Pact.
The hush of Book I ch. 1 and ch. 20 is the girinis listening for the Pact to break.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Game and safe paths to those who ask and repay.
Leads the greedy in circles until they die.
After Šventaragis (1387) and hundreds of other groves, it attaches to the family of the man who swung the axe and follows them for generations.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Salt on the stump, and never take more than you asked.
It may let you go, but it will remember your face.

vilkatas.subtitle: Cursed shape · Samogitian folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] werewolf belief (Olaus Magnus 1555; Herodotus 4.105) · [Saga] two things under one word
Bought power · Velnias's craft sold through raganos (the cursed vilkolakis, not the sworn brotherhood)
The edge of one village; a stump with a knife in it at a crossroads
The way back to human shape, while a human mind lasts
A person's shape and, after a season, their mind. After 1387 whole hamlets of runaways and debtors are turned
A wolf that hangs around one village and will not attack its people; a wolf with human eyes
Bread on a knife-point; the true name; burning the belt that made it

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk use one word for two things. The cursed vilkolakis is real flesh-change by a bargain. The sworn vilkatai of the Dykra are men who do not change shape (only their eldest, rarely). Bread on a knife cures the cursed and only offends a sworn wolf.
Bread is courtesy and iron reminds the flesh it was human. Galminas's beast-rage is a third thing: the Root-Mother's possession of her host.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Raganos sell the change. Forces are not bound by the Law of Truth, which is why real flesh-change is possible at all.
The victim keeps it for a season, then loses it.

sections.title: Costs
entries: You stand within reach of its jaws.
If you are wrong, you have just told a hungry wolf your name.
You must take it from the ragana.
Pulling the knife from the stump
Traps a self-changer as a wolf forever. Someone's son.

vilkatas.source: bestiary.md §12 · iron_wolves.md §5.4 · magic_rules.md §1 · world_graph.json (vilkatas servant_of velnias)

milzinai.subtitle: Sleepers in the land · Baltic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] giants who threw stones, built hill-forts and dwindled (Neringa made the Curonian Spit) · [Saga] asleep in the land
The hills themselves: their bones are the hills; barrows and hill-forts
Nothing. They take no part in events
Nothing, unless you dig into their barrows or move their stones: the earth moves back
Boulders with hand-prints (milžinų akmenys); hill-forts nobody remembers building; tremors under barrows
None needed, and none would work

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk say the giants dwindled into ordinary people. They did not: they sleep, and it is men who dwindled, small enough to bargain.
They are what Lithuania's people were in the age of the first oaths.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Still asleep, but landslips on hill-forts and stones that move between one dawn and the next.

milzinai.source: bestiary.md §13 · Book V epilogue · world_graph.json (milzinai servant_of zemyna)

smakas.subtitle: Dragon-serpent · Baltic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] the slibinas that demands tribute and is slain by a hero; smakas borrowed from Slavic smok · [Saga] a žaltys that grew wrong
Revenant · the dead snake-line, grown beneath a city
Beneath hill-forts, cathedrals and old cellars; the foundations of the Vilnius cathedral after 1387
A whole town's luck; tribute, in daughters
Cattle, and a town's girls. It feeds on the wealth of Vilnius
Cattle vanishing; a town that prospers inexplicably while its girls disappear
Fire and smith's iron (it lives deep); tribute; starving it of luck

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk see a dragon a hero will slay. The truth: a snake-king fed on blood instead of milk, with a žaltys's link to one house's luck swollen into a link with a whole town's. Its demand for maidens is the folk memory of towns paying daughters to keep their prosperity.

The sacred snakes of Šventaragis are killed and thrown unburned into the trench for the new cathedral. Snake-blood in the ground breeds snakes, and blood spilled in hatred breeds a single smakas beneath the bishop's floor.

sections.title: Actions
entries: On the wealth and daughters of the city above it.
The Gold-Glutton and the Root-Mother both want it.

sections.title: Costs
entries: It lives deep. Digging it out means digging up the town.
If the town stops prospering, it weakens. The town stops prospering.

smakas.source: bestiary.md §14 · legends_and_songs.md §2 · world_graph.json (smakas shard_of zaltys) · Book I ch. 29

veles.subtitle: The fed dead · Baltic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] souls of the dead, fed at Vėlinės and Kūčios, imagined as birds on the Birds' Way · [Saga] cremation climbs; the rest linger
Dvasia · the dead who linger, reached through Vėjopatis
The threshold, the empty place at table, the heated pirtis
Food at Vėlinės and Kūčios, their names said, and to be remembered by a child who has forgotten them
A family's best food, every year; a favour in return when they are asked for help
Birds that come too close; a chill at the empty place at table; food that loses its smell overnight
None: they are kin. Stop feeding them and they turn hungry

sections.title: Traits
entries: Cremation is the fastest road up the Glass Mountain to Dausos. The slower-climbing dead linger as vėlės who must be fed. The folk keep the feast as courtesy; it is in fact their food, and when the Church moves it to All Souls and families that convert stop feeding them, the dead turn hungry.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Warn their kin, guard the threshold, sometimes fight. A family with well-fed dead has a hidden army of grandparents.
A fed vėlė can be asked for help, through Vėjopatis.

sections.title: Costs
entries: A family's best food, given every year.
It will ask in return: to be remembered by a child who has forgotten it.

alkanosios_veles.subtitle: The hungry dead · Baltic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] the unmourned, unburied or unfed dead who return, kept busy with scattered poppy seed · [Saga] the same dead, no longer fed
Revenant · the fed dead gone predator
Unconsecrated graves near abandoned groves; cold houses
Warmth first, then the living's memory of the dead one's face, then life: the old and the sick die in its presence
Houses that will not stay warm; a family that cannot remember a grandmother's name; cattle dead in the stall without a mark
Burning the body (the only true cure); poppy seed; a ring of ash

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk say the dead return until set right. The truth: a vėlė no longer fed does not fade. It starves, and starving makes it a predator. The worst are the unburned, who cannot climb at all.
Rare before 1387 (bad deaths only). After it, abandoned groves breed them. This is the saga's central later-book threat.

sections.title: Actions
entries: On warmth, then memory, then life.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Bread, kisielius or beer on the grave and the name spoken. The priest asks why you are feasting on a grave.
Scattered on the path from the grave; they must count it. Buys a night, not a cure.
Renewed nightly. Ordinary ash thins fast; live ash is priceless.
After 1387 a crime and a heresy, and someone always sees the smoke.

vaiduokliai.subtitle: Apparitions · Baltic folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] ghosts, the visible return of the dead · [Saga] the land's memory replaying
Residue · the Law of Memory, not a spirit
Places of great working or great grief: the Krėva cell, the Palanga stone
Nothing. Most have no one inside
Nothing, beyond wasted offerings from those who mistake one for a vėlė
The same figure at the same hour. Amber shows them most clearly, because amber stores memory
None needed. To lay one, change the place

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk confuse them with vėlės. A vėlė can use one as a mask, but most apparitions are pictures with no one inside, so most ghosts cannot be fed or bargained with.
Unchanged in nature, but the Unbinding is a century of grief, and grief leaves pictures.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Shows the same strong feeling, at the same place and hour.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Burn the room or fell the tree. The memory goes with it.

vaiduokliai.source: bestiary.md §17 · magic_rules.md §5.3 · world_graph.json (pebble anchors vaiduokliai) · Book I ch. 23

velnio_pavidalai.subtitle: Velnias's small shapes · Lithuanian folk tales, saga-true
fields: [Record] Velnias as a gentleman in green, a black cat or a black dog, regularly cheated by peasants · [Saga] velniukai, small change from the same purse
Dvasia · shards of Velnias; the Shadow-Seller's scouts
Villages, mills, swamps and stones; after 1387 the towns where ledgers make better bargains
Small deals, and to learn what a prince will need
Bargains kept to the letter, paid later
A black cat the day before a quarrel; a stranger in a too-fine green coat at a wedding who will not dance (he would show his foot); a dog that will not leave in a thunderstorm
Thunder-stones; after 1387 the Candlemas thunder candle lit in storms

sections.title: Traits
entries: These are not the Shadow-Seller himself, but small change from the same purse. Hungry and fair like their lord, they keep every deal to the letter and lose to anyone cleverer.
The Shadow-Seller uses them as eyes: a black dog at the edge of the firelight is often how he learns what a prince will need.

sections.title: Actions
entries: With the Krivis and the vaidilutės gone, they are the only teachers left to many raganos.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Rudeness to strangers is itself a sin against custom, so you may insult the Beggar by mistake.
Draft the deal yourself. If you are less clever than you think, the letter is your ruin.

velnio_pavidalai.source: bestiary.md §20 · legends_and_songs.md §8, §9 · cosmology.md §3.1 · Book I ch. 8-9

pincuikas.subtitle: Clerk of small bargains · literary devil, saga-true
fields: [Record] a minor devil best known from Boruta's *Baltaragio malūnas* (1945); folk currency of the name uncertain · [Saga] the Shadow-Seller's clerk
Dvasia · a named velniukas, Henė's go-between
Small bargains with millers, sextons and serving-maids; to keep the threads that bind them
Small obligations (threads) from the small. A miller's debt; a hidden guard's sleeping-place (Kirmėlė, 1382)
A dapper little man who knows everyone's debts; a stammering, polite voice behind a door; a ledger
Make him write the bargain down and read it back aloud

sections.title: Traits
entries: No old belief to correct: the folk name is thinly attested. In the saga he is fussy, polite and fond of mills. He is the reason Henė always knows who in a castle can be bought.
Before 1387 one clerk among many. After it, the Unbinding is a boom time for small bargains.

sections.title: Actions
entries: He makes the small deals while Henė makes the great ones with princes.
Kirmėlė sold Kęstutis's hidden guard through him in 1382 to save his village, and the village burned anyway. In Book II ch. 5 he sold Skirgaila the plot of 1389 for a miller's debt.

sections.title: Costs
entries: He cannot resist reading aloud, but you must be able to spot the trick when he does.
Never let him name the price later. He will refuse the bargain, and you will not get what you came for.

pincuikas.source: bestiary.md §21 · iron_wolves.md §13 (Kirmėlė) · world_graph.json (pincuikas servant_of shadow_seller) · Book II ch. 5 · Book VI ch. 27

ragana.subtitle: Seer-witch · Lithuanian folk belief, saga-true
fields: [Record] the witch (from regėti, to see), gathering on Šatrija hill at Midsummer, also a healer · [Saga] a woman born with Kalba outside the priestly lines
A woman alone at the edge of the village whom everyone visits and no one invites
Her price, in full, plus silence. After 1387, a teacher
Her own costs (blindness, voicelessness, thirst), passed on in her prices
Dew-marks dragged through the rye on Rasos morning; cows dry for no reason
Rowan over the cowshed, iron in the churn, juniper smoke

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk are right that she sees and can harm. They are wrong that she serves Velnias, at least before 1387. After it, with the Krivis and the vaidilutės gone, his small shapes are the only teachers left.
After 1387 she is the only defence against the hungry dead, and the first one blamed for them.

sections.title: Actions
entries: She works by Kalba and pays the price herself, so she charges heavily.
Curse-belts for the vilkolakis are Velnias's craft sold through raganos.
Book II ch. 9: a Lagoon ragana offers to draw the poison from the hostage boys over any distance, but her old body cannot carry it, so it must go into a young Order child. Vytautas refuses.

sections.title: Costs
entries: What she asks, plus your silence, plus the risk that you will need her again.
Small, but she will know you did it.

ragana.source: bestiary.md §22 · power_systems.md §4 · magic_rules.md §4.1 · Book II ch. 9 · prologue

gelezinis_vilkas.subtitle: Omen-entity · chronicle legend, saga-true
fields: [Record] Gediminas's dream, read by Lizdeika (16th-century chronicles) · [Saga] the collared spirit of the Gediminid house
Omen-entity · cannot be met, fought or fed
The Šventaragis hill, Trakai island and its lake, the deep forest
Nothing. It howls from grief, not hunger
Nothing. It gives knowledge, which is the cost
Thousands of wolves howling at once; a wolf of grey iron glimpsed in mist on an island or hill; frost on iron in summer

sections.title: Traits
entries: The folk (and Lizdeika's public reading) say a castle and a famous city. The Krivis's version: iron because collared, and its hundred voices are the house's own sons and grandsons tearing at one another. The folk attach the omen to Vytautas himself, which is half right.
The wolves that answer it are the dead sworn vilkatai, laid in the bogs and never burned. The brotherhood keeps the one physical relic of the dream, the skull.

sections.title: Actions
entries: At the turning points of Gediminid fate: a Gediminid betrayed, kneeling at a foreign altar, or dead.
Seen dissolving into mist on Trakai island when the Last Flame dies (1430). Its last howl rises from the Trakai lake in 1440.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Those who hear it learn their master's fate, not their own.

nedegintieji.subtitle: The Unburned · saga invention (the Unbinding)
fields: [Saga] the crusade dead: Lithuanians pit-buried by the Order, and the Order's own dead in pagan ground, risen after 1387
Revenant · hungry vėlės crossed with the Iron Saint's appetite
Mass graves near old Reise routes; abandoned groves
Warmth, hearth to hearth. They do not eat
Warmth: a village they pass through is left with fires that will not catch
Lines of frost-prints in a summer field; groves left untended
Fire (only cremation stops one for good); live ash in a ring

sections.title: Traits
entries: There is no folk belief to be wrong: the nearest, that the unburied return, is right but small. These march as well as hunger. Cold and silent, they walk in the formation they died in, pagan and Christian side by side, still carrying their wounds.
The commonest serious threat of Books II-V. After Pabaiskas (1435) the field holds thousands.

sections.title: Actions
entries: They move from hearth to hearth.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Heresy, and a whole pit takes cartloads of wood and a day nobody can hide.
If anyone remembers the names. No one does.

reizos_raiteliai.subtitle: Riders of the Reise · saga invention (the Iron Saint)
fields: [Saga] knights who died on Reise in complete fearless conviction and did not stop
The old Reise routes through the Wildnis, along the Neman and into Samogitia; before 1387 Prussia only
Nothing. They do not hunger, they repeat
Everything in their path, as they once did
Furnace heat in winter; crosses that ring like anvils; hoof-prints that steam in snow; mail that never rusts
Unfrozen running water; smith's iron forged at a pagan hearth; standing still without fear

sections.title: Traits
entries: No folk belief to correct. The saga truth: they ride on the anniversary of their death, through villages without seeing them, smelling of quench-water and hot iron. Before 1387 the Pact kept them harmlessly in Prussia.
They strengthen before Grunwald and scream when the Iron Saint breaks. In Book V ch. 14 they break at the unfrozen river at Pabaiskas.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Ride the old routes and kill everything in the path.

sections.title: Costs
entries: They cannot cross it unfrozen, but in winter everything is frozen.
Bog-iron does nothing and feast-day iron feeds them. Few such smiths remain after 1387.
They see only fear and pass the fearless by. Almost nobody manages it.

bebalsiai.subtitle: The Voiceless · saga invention (the White Silence)
fields: [Saga] built on the chroniclers' report of white baptismal shirts given in 1387; some came for the shirt, not the faith
Victims · the White Silence's hollowed ones
Villages along the Neris around Vilnius first; after 1413 Samogitia
Nothing: they are not monsters. The White Silence listens through them
Their own voice, then shadow, then warmth. Where several gather, sound dies
Frost flowers in their footprints; people who stop speaking after a mass baptism; villages where nobody sings
Real belief in anything; the victim's old name spoken by a living fire

sections.title: Traits
entries: No folk belief to correct. The saga truth: the White Silence gathers wherever a baptism is bought, and a bought baptism is the opening. It settles into the empty place where neither old custom nor new faith lives.
In numbers they smother Wind workings and freeze Water ones.

sections.title: Actions
entries: Hollowed over months, they let the Force hear.

sections.title: Costs
entries: An honest Christian or an honest pagan cannot become one. Belief cannot be forced, and that is the whole problem.
Returns the voice for a night. The White Silence notices who did it.

uzgesiles.subtitle: The Quenched · saga invention (killed flames)
fields: [Saga] born of killed sacred flames: sparks of Šventaragis, cut off from Gabija in 1387
Hearths; worst near Vilnius and around every grove-flame put out
Every flame they find. A house with užgesėlės cannot keep its hearth lit, which in winter is death
Hearths that go out every night; blue glints in cold ash; children always cold
Live ash from a still-kept flame; Gabija's own words

sections.title: Traits
entries: No folk belief to correct. They are not malicious: tiny blue sparks that remember being fire and swallow every flame they find.
They exist only after 1387 and multiply with every flame put out (the Samogitian alkai, 1413-17).

sections.title: Actions
entries: They nest in hearths and swallow the flame.

sections.title: Costs
entries: Scattered in the hearth, it gives them what they want and they go out content. After 1387 the only kept flame is Vytautas's, and every pinch is a risk to its keeper.
A caster at the hearth pays exhaustion and soul-chill.
No live ash: the hearths of Trakai fail one by one (Book V ch. 4).

skaiciuotojas.subtitle: The Counter · saga invention (the Gold-Glutton)
fields: [Saga] a spirit of the Gold-Glutton, formed where ledgers, tolls and land sold by the furlong gather
Voice · Aukso Rijūnas's servant, never a body
Tollhouses, counting-rooms, Order commanderies, Hanseatic factories; the Lutsk congress chamber
Care: those who listen too long begin to see one another as sums, and are left prosperous and hollow. It does not kill
Coins that are always warm; a voice under the floor of a counting-house; merchants who have stopped caring for their children and cannot say why

sections.title: Traits
entries: No folk belief to correct. Soft and pleasant, it counts the coins in the room, then the goods, then the people, then the years each has left.
Before 1387 confined to Order and Hanseatic towns. After it, everywhere money changes hands, dominant in Book IV.

sections.title: Actions
entries: In a soft monotone, until the listener counts too.
Hears it for thirty years and learns to carry it like a pebble in the boot (Book IV ch. 16).

sections.title: Costs
entries: Giving something away without counting it silences the Counter in that room. You must truly not count, and it makes counting feel like breathing.
Counting and singing cannot share a room. Merchants rarely sing.

ausrine.subtitle: The morning star · a figure of the Moon's daina; no cult recorded
fields: The morning star (Venus); the unpunished third party of the Moon's marriage
God (Layer I) · Dangus; no element, no Force-face

sections.title: Answers
entries: A figure of folk myth only. She does not act, speak or appear.
In the saga's law the oath-breaker is cut and the seducer goes free. Book II can use that (Jogaila is a Mėnuo, Jadvyga an Aušrinė).
